requirements.title: Mutex/condvar primitives provide mutual exclusion and signaling
requirements.text: rcp_mutex_init/lock/unlock/destroy() and rcp_cond_init/wait/timedwait_until/signal/broadcast/destroy() shall provide standard mutual-exclusion and condition-variable signaling semantics on every supported platform (POSIX pthreads and Win32), used by every module that needs cross-thread synchronization.

requirements.title: rcp_thread_start()/rcp_thread_start_detached() launch a new thread
requirements.text: rcp_thread_start() and rcp_thread_start_detached() shall start a new OS thread running the given function with the given argument, on every supported platform, with rcp_thread_start_detached() releasing any OS resources needed to join it later since the caller will never join it.

requirements.title: rcp_monotonic_ms() returns a monotonically non-decreasing clock reading
requirements.text: rcp_monotonic_ms() shall return a millisecond-resolution timestamp from a monotonic clock source (unaffected by wall-clock adjustments) on every supported platform, used codebase-wide for deadline/timeout computation.

requirements.title: rcp_wire_error_t assigns the governing spec's own numbered wire error codes
requirements.text: rcp_wire_error_t shall assign each of the seventeen numbered error codes 1-17 the exact numeric value the governing TC18 Remote Control Protocol Specification's own error-code table assigns it, plus a value-0 RCP_ERROR_NONE sentinel (this implementation's own addition, not part of the spec's table) for "no applicable wire code".

requirements.title: rcp_wire_error_string() returns a unique, non-empty message per code
requirements.text: rcp_wire_error_string() shall return a unique, non-empty, human-readable description for every defined rcp_wire_error_t constant, and a non-NULL, non-empty generic message for any other value.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wire_error() maps a CRC mismatch to POCI_FAILURE
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wire_error() shall return RCP_ERROR_POCI_FAILURE for RCP_E2E_ERR_CRC_MISMATCH -- the code the governing spec's own numbered error-code table assigns a CRC mismatch -- and RCP_ERROR_NONE for every other rcp_e2e_errc_t value, since neither RCP_E2E_OK nor RCP_E2E_ERR_SHORT_FRAME has a wire-error-code counterpart.

requirements.title: rcp_udp_annexj_wrap() prepends a 4-octet big-endian sequence number
requirements.text: rcp_udp_annexj_wrap() shall heap-allocate a buffer holding a 4-octet big-endian encapsulation sequence number followed by the given AVTPDU bytes, and return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data=NULL) on allocation failure.

requirements.title: rcp_udp_annexj_unwrap() strips the sequence number and borrows the AVTPDU
requirements.text: rcp_udp_annexj_unwrap() shall read the leading 4-octet big-endian sequence number from a wrap()-produced buffer and point the caller at the AVTPDU bytes that follow (borrowed, not copied), returning false without touching any output parameter when the supplied buffer is shorter than RCP_UDP_ANNEX_J_SEQ_LEN.

requirements.title: send() applies the Annex J encapsulation sequence number automatically
requirements.text: A UDP AVTP transport's send() shall prepend its own per-connection monotonically-incrementing sequence number (via rcp_udp_annexj_wrap()) to every AVTPDU before it reaches the socket, transparently to the rcp_avtp_transport_t caller.

requirements.title: recv() strips the Annex J encapsulation sequence number automatically
requirements.text: A UDP AVTP transport's recv() shall strip the leading Annex J encapsulation sequence number (via rcp_udp_annexj_unwrap()) before returning a received AVTPDU to the caller, dropping (and continuing to wait for the next datagram on) any received datagram shorter than the sequence number field itself; rcp_udp_avtp_transport_last_recv_seq() shall report the sequence number of the most recently successfully received datagram, or 0 if none has been received yet.

requirements.title: dial()/bind()_default_port() target the Annex J control port
requirements.text: rcp_udp_avtp_transport_dial_default_port() and rcp_udp_avtp_transport_bind_default_port() shall behave exactly as rcp_udp_avtp_transport_dial()/_bind() called with port == RCP_UDP_ANNEX_J_CONTROL_PORT (17221).

requirements.title: rcp_l2_frame_encode() builds dst+src+EtherType+AVTPDU framing
requirements.text: rcp_l2_frame_encode() shall heap-allocate a buffer holding the given destination MAC (6 octets), source MAC (6 octets), RCP_L2_ETHERTYPE (2 octets, big-endian), and the given AVTPDU bytes, in that order, and return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data=NULL) on allocation failure.

requirements.title: rcp_l2_frame_decode() validates EtherType and borrows the AVTPDU
requirements.text: rcp_l2_frame_decode() shall return false, leaving every output parameter untouched, when the supplied frame is shorter than RCP_L2_HEADER_LEN or its EtherType field is not RCP_L2_ETHERTYPE; otherwise it shall populate the destination/source MAC outputs and point the caller at the AVTPDU bytes that follow (borrowed, not copied).

requirements.title: rcp_l2_avtp_transport_new() never returns NULL except on allocation failure
requirements.text: rcp_l2_avtp_transport_new() shall return a non-NULL rcp_avtp_transport_t on any failure to open/bind the underlying raw socket or read the interface's own hardware address, with ok() reporting false in that case; it shall return NULL only on this module's own allocation failure.

requirements.title: ok() distinguishes a successful open from a socket/bind/ioctl failure
requirements.text: rcp_l2_avtp_transport_ok() shall return true only for a transport whose underlying raw socket was created, bound to its interface, and had that interface's own hardware address successfully read, all successfully.

requirements.title: local_mac() reports the transport's own interface-derived source MAC
requirements.text: rcp_l2_avtp_transport_local_mac() shall write the network interface's own hardware address (read once at construction time, never caller-supplied) into the caller's buffer and return true for an ok() transport, or return false without writing anything for a transport that is not ok().

requirements.title: send() frames outgoing AVTPDUs with the caller-supplied destination MAC
requirements.text: An L2 AVTP transport's send() shall wrap each AVTPDU via rcp_l2_frame_encode() using the transport's own caller-supplied destination MAC and interface-derived source MAC before transmitting it on the underlying raw socket, and shall return RCP_ERR_CLOSED once close() has been called.

requirements.title: recv() decodes AVTP-over-Ethernet frames and ignores its own transmitted copies
requirements.text: An L2 AVTP transport's recv() shall decode each received frame via rcp_l2_frame_decode(), returning only its AVTPDU bytes to the caller, and shall ignore (continue waiting past) any frame the underlying raw socket reports as this same socket's own locally-transmitted outgoing copy rather than a frame genuinely received from the wire.

requirements.title: close() unblocks a concurrent in-progress recv() without invalidating the fd
requirements.text: Calling close() on an L2 transport while a different thread is blocked inside that same transport's recv() shall cause that recv() call to return RCP_ERR_CLOSED within one poll slice, without the underlying raw socket being invalidated out from under it; the fd itself shall only be closed once destroy() runs.

requirements.title: Non-Linux stub: ok() false and every operation fails without crashing
requirements.text: On a non-Linux platform, rcp_l2_avtp_transport_new() shall return a non-NULL transport whose ok() reports false and whose send()/recv() return RCP_ERR_CLOSED without crashing, exactly matching udp.c's own Windows stub convention.

requirements.title: Missing CAP_NET_RAW/root leaves the transport cleanly not-ok()
requirements.text: When the calling process lacks CAP_NET_RAW (and is not root), rcp_l2_avtp_transport_new()'s underlying raw-socket open shall fail and the returned transport's ok() shall report false, without crashing or requiring the caller to pre-check its own privilege level.

requirements.title: rcp_compound_start_condition_met() implements the "any state" start_state sentinel
requirements.text: rcp_compound_start_condition_met() shall return true iff step->sequencer_index is rcp_sequencer_index_valid() for table and either step->start_state is zero (the request starts in whatever state the sequencer currently holds) or table's current state at that index equals step->start_state, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.1 ("If cmp_start_state = 0 then the request shall be started in any state unless the sequencer is disabled"). It shall return false for an index the table does not hold, including when start_state is zero.

requirements.title: rcp_timed_decode_request() rejects a non-zero reserved octet
requirements.text: rcp_timed_decode_request() shall return RCP_TIMED_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO when the reserved octet at offset 1 of the repurposed message_timestamp region carries any set bit, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected").

requirements.title: rcp_timed_decode_request() rejects a timed request with hs or cs set
requirements.text: rcp_timed_decode_request() shall return RCP_TIMED_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD when the decoded byte_message_info hs or cs bit is set, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("hs, cs -- All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD").

requirements.title: rcp_timed_due() reports whether a presentation_time has arrived
requirements.text: rcp_timed_due() shall return true iff presentation_time is at or before now in the same wrapping 48-bit domain rcp_timed_too_far() uses, i.e. iff the request's execution condition is satisfied.

requirements.title: rcp_chained_exec_delay_elapsed() compares elapsed against chain_exec_delay
requirements.text: rcp_chained_exec_delay_elapsed() shall return true iff elapsed >= chain_exec_delay, both expressed in multiples of the addressed endpoint's configured ep_delay_time and measured from the moment the member's predecessor finalized (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Table 9).

requirements.title: rcp_chained_decode_member() rejects a non-zero reserved sub-field octet
requirements.text: rcp_chained_decode_member() shall return RCP_CHAINED_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO when any of octets 1-3 or 6-7 of the repurposed message_timestamp region carries a set bit, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Table 9.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() routes each request by its own request_type
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() shall classify each arriving ACF message by peeking its repurposed request_type opcode and passing it to rcp_sched_classify(), and shall route it accordingly: a message that is not a repurposed-timestamp ACF_GBB, or whose opcode this build does not recognize, shall take the rcp_server_endpoint_submit() path unchanged and report RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_EXECUTE_NOW or RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_QUEUED; a cancellation opcode shall report RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_CANCELLATION without being stored; every other conditional kind shall be decoded and stored, reporting RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_PENDING. *out_request_type shall always be written -- the opcode byte for a conditional or cancellation request, 0 otherwise.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() rejects an undecodable or unstorable conditional request
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() shall return RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_REJECTED, storing nothing and leaving the request store's occupancy unchanged, when a message whose opcode claims a conditional request kind fails that kind's own decode_* validation, or when the store already holds RCP_SERVER_MAX_PENDING requests.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() evaluates each stored request against its own execution condition
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() shall report a stored request as due only when that request kind's own condition holds: a compound or compound-wait request requires rcp_compound_start_condition_met() against ctx->sequencers and rcp_compound_exec_delay_elapsed() since it first held (a compound-wait additionally requiring ctx->wait_condition_met); a triggered request requires rcp_triggered_threshold_reached(), rcp_triggered_exec_delay_elapsed() since the threshold was reached, and ctx->endpoint_idle; a timed request requires ctx->gptp_locked and rcp_timed_due() against ctx->gptp_now; a chained request requires its predecessor to have finalized, rcp_chained_exec_delay_elapsed() since that instant, and ctx->endpoint_idle. It shall report no request as due when none qualifies.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() holds safety-tagged requests back until the safe state is reached
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() shall report a stored request whose request_type is safety-tagged (MSB set, 0x8x) as due only when rcp_e2e_request_may_execute(request_type, ctx->in_safe_state) permits it, i.e. only once ctx->in_safe_state is true, regardless of whether that request's own execution condition is otherwise satisfied. A non-safety-tagged request shall be unaffected by ctx->in_safe_state.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() returns the highest-priority due request
requirements.text: When more than one stored request is due at once, rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() shall return the one that rcp_sched_compare() orders first over {kind, arrival sequence}: the higher rcp_sched_kind_rank() first, and among requests of equal rank the earliest admitted.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_complete() applies the executed request's own completion action
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_complete() shall, for a compound request, apply rcp_compound_tick() and, for a compound-wait request, rcp_compound_wait_tick() against ctx->sequencers, so that the sequencer is advanced only when the advance guard still holds. It shall not advance any sequencer for a triggered, timed, or chained request.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_complete() applies the repetition rule
requirements.text: After the completion action, rcp_server_endpoint_complete() shall leave a request whose repeat_count is the all-ones infinite sentinel in the store with its repeat_count unchanged, shall remove a request whose repeat_count is zero, and shall otherwise decrement repeat_count by one and leave the request in the store re-armed (its start condition to be satisfied afresh before it may run again). Timed and chained requests carry no repetition sub-field and shall always be removed. It shall return true iff the request remains in the store.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_notify_trigger() routes an occurrence to every matching stored request
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_notify_trigger() shall offer the observed (source_ep, signal_nr) occurrence to every stored triggered request via rcp_triggered_runtime_record_occurrence(), so that only requests whose own trigger_source_ep/trigger_signal_nr match count it, and shall return how many counted it.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_chain_predecessor_done() starts a chained request's delay at the predecessor's finalization
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_chain_predecessor_done() shall mark the stored chained request at index as having its predecessor finalized and record now as the instant its chain_exec_delay is measured from, and shall not restart that timer on any later evaluation. It shall return false, changing nothing, when index does not name a stored chained request.

requirements.title: The cancellation functions remove exactly the requests their own opcode names
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_all() shall remove every stored conditional request and return how many; rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_single() shall report rcp_cancel_attempt()'s outcome and remove the stored request whose transaction_num equals clear_transaction_num only when that outcome is RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_CANCELED; rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_non_safestate() shall remove every stored request that is not safety-tagged, leaving the safety-tagged ones in place, and return how many were removed. Each shall free the byte copy of every request it removes.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_watchdog_purge() keeps only the safety sequence
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_watchdog_purge() shall remove from the request store exactly those requests rcp_e2e_watchdog_purge_should_keep() does not keep -- i.e. every non-safety-tagged one -- and return how many were removed, so that only the safety sequence survives a watchdog overflow to drive the endpoint into its configured safe state.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() routes a request through the request_type-aware admission path
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() shall, after rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() admission and endpoint lookup, route the request through rcp_server_endpoint_admit() and map its outcome onto RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_OK (running the endpoint's handler synchronously), _QUEUED, _PENDING, _CANCELLED (having applied the named cancellation against that endpoint's request store), or _REJECTED. A standard request shall behave exactly as before: executed immediately when the endpoint is enabled, queued when it is not.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_t owns the sequencer-state table compound requests read
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_set_sequencer_count() shall replace and free any sequencer table the server already held with a freshly allocated rcp_sequencer_table_new(count), and rcp_mock_server_sequencers() shall return that table. A server whose table is the unsupported ({NULL,0}) one shall never report a compound or compound-wait request as due.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_tick() executes at most one due conditional request
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_tick() shall select the highest-priority due stored request on the addressed endpoint via rcp_server_endpoint_select_due(), run that request's own stored frame through that endpoint's registered handler, finalize it via rcp_server_endpoint_complete(), and return true. It shall return false, leaving *out_response zeroed and executing nothing, when the byte_bus_id names no endpoint or no stored request is due.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_tick() evaluates conditions against the server's own sequencer table
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_tick() shall evaluate execution conditions against the server's own sequencer table, ignoring and overwriting any sequencers pointer the caller supplied in ctx, so a caller cannot have a request evaluated against a table the server does not own.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_notify_trigger() reaches every endpoint
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_notify_trigger() shall offer the observed (source_ep, signal_nr) occurrence to every registered endpoint's request store, since a triggered request stored on one endpoint routinely waits on a different endpoint's trigger signal, and shall return the total number of stored requests that counted it.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() applies chain sequencing across a frame's members in order
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() shall, for each chained member it encounters, call rcp_chained_advance() with whether any request precedes it in this frame, whether that predecessor finalized with an error, and that member's own cs bit -- reporting RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_CHAIN_ERROR for a chained member with no predecessor and RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_CHAIN_ABORTED for one the chain state excludes, in both cases without dispatching that member to its endpoint. rcp_mock_server_watchdog_purge() shall apply rcp_server_endpoint_watchdog_purge() to the addressed endpoint and return how many requests it purged.

requirements.title: acf_msg_type constants carry the specification's own numeric values
requirements.text: RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB shall equal 0x0E and RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB shall equal 0x0D, the acf_msg_type values TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 and §11.2.2.1 Table 6 assign to the abbreviated byte bus (ACF_ABB) and generic byte bus (ACF_GBB) message formats respectively.

requirements.title: read_size/segment_num interpretation is selected by the op bit
requirements.text: The 12-bit read_size_or_segment_num field of byte_message_info shall be interpreted as read_size when the op bit is 0 (RCP_ACF_OP_READ, a request expecting a data response) and as segment_num otherwise, per TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 and §11.2.2.1 Table 6. c-RCP shall expose that selection to callers rather than leaving the field an uninterpreted round-tripped slot.

requirements.title: The 3-state rcp_acf_op_t maps onto the specification's single op bit
requirements.text: rcp_acf_encode_abb()/rcp_acf_encode_gbb() shall encode op as the single wire bit TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 defines -- 0b when the sender expects a response with data (RCP_ACF_OP_READ) and 1b when it does not (RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE and the encode-only convenience value RCP_ACF_OP_NONE, which is indistinguishable from RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE on the wire) -- and rcp_acf_decode_abb()/rcp_acf_decode_gbb() shall therefore never produce RCP_ACF_OP_NONE from decoded input.

requirements.title: byte_bus_id is 11 bits on the wire; c-RCP represents only the low 8
requirements.text: byte_message_info's byte_bus_id field is 11 bits wide on the wire (byte_bus_id[10:8] in octet 2 bits 2:0 and byte_bus_id[7:0] in octet 3), per TC18 §11.2.1 Figure 7 / Table 4. c-RCP's rcp_byte_bus_id_t represents only the low 8 bits: rcp_acf_unpack_header() shall return RCP_ACF_ERR_BUS_ID_OVERFLOW, rather than silently truncating, for any wire value whose byte_bus_id[10:8] is nonzero. NOT FULLY IMPLEMENTED: endpoint identifiers 256-2047 cannot be addressed or represented at all.

requirements.title: A request carries rsv=00b, hs=0b, cs=0b, rsp=0b and err=0b unless its own kind assigns the bit a meaning
requirements.text: An encoded RCP request shall carry rsv = 00b, hs = 0b, err = 0b, and rsp = 0b (rsp = 0b is what identifies an ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB message as a request rather than a response), and cs = 0b except where the request kind assigns cs its own meaning (compound-wait per TC18 §11.2.2.2 Table 7, chained per §11.2.2.4 Table 9); a received message whose rsp bit is set shall not be admitted as a request. c-RCP currently forces only rsv to zero and round-trips hs, cs, rsp and err without constraint.

requirements.title: The evt[2:0]=111b EP_func configuration request is implemented for PWM_OUT only
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request — evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data — usable against EVERY endpoint type either through the RC Server (EP0) register map or directly by byte_bus_id. c-RCP implements this shape for exactly one endpoint type: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_pwm.c:206), which decodes a 16-bit big-endian relative start address plus data octets. Every other endpoint type (GPIO, SPI, I2C, UART, LIN, CAN, ADC, ISELED, MDIO, wakeup) exposes no EP_func addressed-write path, and no server-side dispatcher classifies an incoming evt==7 request as a configuration request and routes it to the addressed endpoint. Consequence: endpoint functional configuration is unreachable over the wire for all but PWM_OUT.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18, TC18.txt L2464-2466, L2473-2479

requirements.title: Every endpoint must publish EP_LEN at EP_func offset 0x00 and ignore a write overrunning it
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.1 requires that every endpoint publish its EP_LEN parameter at EP_func relative start_address 0x00, and that any byte_msg_payload whose length plus start_address exceeds EP_LEN be ignored in its entirety. c-RCP satisfies this for PWM_OUT only — RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_pwm.h:361) and the out-of-range rejection at src/ep_pwm.c:224. No other endpoint type in c-RCP defines an EP_LEN register or enforces the overrun rule, because no other endpoint type has an addressed EP_func write path at all. Consequence: the specification's one universal bounds check on configuration writes exists at exactly one of the eleven endpoint types.

requirements.title: A discovery request while the discovery stream is already claimed is answered with a stream-occupied error
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not report a discovery-stream-occupied condition (TC18 §12.3, Figure 16). rcp_discovery_claim_note_request() is a void function that silently declines to preempt a held claim, so a caller cannot tell a granted claim from a refused one, and there is no DISCOVERY_STREAM_OCCUPIED error code in rcp_error_code_t to send back. A second RC Client attempting discovery in HW_UNCONFIGURED or HW_CONFIGURED gets no indication that another client owns the configuration stream.

requirements.title: per-stream sequence-number enforcement (rx_enforce_seq)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement the rx_enforce_seq gate (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000D bit 1, 1 bit, R/W*), under which a request shall only be filed for execution if the sequence number carried in its AVTPDU has increased relative to the previously accepted request on that stream. Neither rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t nor e2e.h carries the configuration bit or the per-stream sequence-counter state it would gate. Consequence: a replayed or reordered AVTPDU is filed and executed exactly like a fresh one, defeating the specification's own anti-replay/ordering safety measure; include/rcp/e2e.h:229-240 acknowledges this gap and notes that tara.md/CYBERSECURITY.md still cite the removed REQ-E2E-004..012 replay mitigations.

requirements.title: sequence-error safe-state escalation (rx_seq_safestate_enable)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement rx_seq_safestate_enable (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000D bit 2, 1 bit, R/W*), under which a detected sequence-number discontinuity (a Sequence_Nr that did not advance by a single increment) shall bring all endpoints bound to that request stream into their configured safe state. c-RCP has neither the detection (see the rx_enforce_seq gap) nor the escalation: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() computes enter_safe_state from the watchdog only. Consequence: an interrupted or tampered request sequence produces no safe-state transition, so the only safety net configured through Table 22 that does not depend on a watchdog timeout is entirely absent.

requirements.title: request-storage-overflow safe-state escalation (rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000D bit 5, 1 bit, R/W*), under which an overflow of any one endpoint's request storage shall bring all endpoints bound to that request stream into their configured safe state. server.h already detects the condition (a request-store-full admission outcome, include/rcp/server.h:216) but drops the request silently and never escalates. Consequence: an endpoint whose request storage is overrun loses requests with no configured safety reaction, so a client flooding one endpoint can silently desynchronize an entire stream's endpoint set.

requirements.title: GPIO request payload is exactly four bytes, mapped LSB-first for endpoints with fewer than 32 pins
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_write_request() and rcp_ep_gpio_decode_request() shall reject any GPIO request whose byte_msg_payload is not exactly RCP_EP_GPIO_PAYLOAD_LEN (4) octets with RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_BAD_PAYLOAD_LEN -- the condition TC18 13.7.4.1 answers on the wire with error code INVALID_PARAMETER -- and an endpoint supporting fewer than RCP_EP_GPIO_MAX_PINS (32) pins shall map its pins onto the least-significant bits of that 32-bit payload.

requirements.title: GPIO trigger signal numbering (Table 40)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP implements the three GPIO trigger conditions (rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() for change, rising and falling edges) but assigns them no trigger signal numbers, so TC18 Table 40's numbering -- signal 0 'GPIO EP request execution done' and, for each pin IOn, signal 3n+1 change / 3n+2 rising / 3n+3 falling up to signal 96 for IO31 falling -- is not represented. A triggered request naming a Table 40 signal number cannot be resolved by this library.

requirements.title: GPIO functional-config registers: base clock, divider and per-pin debounce (Table 41)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_t models only the shared EP prefix plus per-pin (pin_property, trigger); it carries none of TC18 Table 41's gpio_base_clk (0x0004, kHz), gpio_clk_divider (0x0008), gpio_ep_status (0x0006) or the 32 per-pin gpio_debounce_IOn registers (0x0009..0x0024), and implements no debounce filtering at all -- so the rule that n>0 requires n consecutive equal samples, taken off the divided base clock independently of requests, before an input value changes is not enforced.

requirements.title: GPIO response timing: immediate for a pure read, post-debounce otherwise
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 13.7.4.3's GPIO response-timing rule -- a read request carrying no byte_msg_payload generates its response immediately on execution, while a payload-bearing read or any write first changes the pin drive and only then, after the configured debounce time has elapsed, produces its response. Debounce is not modeled (see the Table 41 gap), so both cases respond identically.

requirements.title: I2C functional-config registers beyond i2c_mode, and the missing Ultra-fast preset
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): c-RCP's rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_t models TC18 Table 46 only as i2c_mode. i2c_clock_divider (0x0006), i2c_trail (0x0008, minimum trail time between two transactions in I2C clock cycles), i2c_base_clk and i2c_ep_status are absent, and rcp_ep_i2c_mode_valid() accepts only presets 0..3 -- Ultra-fast mode (value 4, 5 Mbit/s) is rejected as invalid. Table 46 numbers two distinct rows '3' (High-speed 1.7 and 3.4 Mbit/s), an ambiguity ep_i2c.h resolves conservatively in favour of the lower numbering.

requirements.title: I2C payload carries the address and the endpoint stays address-format agnostic
requirements.text: The I2C endpoint's request codec shall treat the byte_msg_payload as the complete I2C payload INCLUDING the target address and shall not interpret, validate or rewrite that address -- remaining transparent to whether the transfer uses a 7-bit or a 10-bit address, per TC18 13.7.7.3.

requirements.title: A lifecycle-state change is refused with EPs_NOT_IDLE while any other endpoint is busy
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not gate lifecycle-state changes on endpoint idleness (TC18 §12.3, Figure 16). rcp_lifecycle_transition() performs the demotion to RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED unconditionally and has no per-endpoint idle input, so a demotion (or a promotion to HW_CONFIGURED) is accepted while other endpoints still have in-flight or queued requests, instead of being rejected with an EPs_NOT_IDLE error response. Requests in flight on unrelated endpoints can therefore be torn down mid-execution by a lifecycle reset.

requirements.title: Endpoint-generic and response-queue configuration are locked alongside HW_config in HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP locks only the HW-generic field kind once the server leaves HW_UNCONFIGURED (TC18 §12.3, Figure 16; §12.3.1.2). rcp_lifecycle_field_kind_t has no kind covering the endpoint generic configuration (rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_t) or the response-queue/request-queue configuration (rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t), so rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() cannot deny a write to those blocks in HW_CONFIGURED or RCP_CONFIGURED. Queue sizing and endpoint pin/type assignment can be changed after the plausibility check that validated them.

requirements.title: A write to a locked configuration register is answered with a locked-config error response
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP never turns a denied configuration write into an error response (TC18 §12.3, Figure 16). rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() returns only a bool, and no requirement or code path maps that denial to an error response carrying RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS. A client whose configuration write was silently dropped cannot distinguish a locked register from a lost frame.

requirements.title: Requests on an unknown stream/byte_bus_id are ignored in HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not drop requests arriving on an unknown stream_id/byte_bus_id combination (TC18 §12.3, Figure 16). rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() takes no stream identity and returns true for every frame in HW_CONFIGURED and RCP_CONFIGURED that survives the TSCF rule, so a frame from an unconfigured stream is admitted to the dispatch path instead of being ignored without response. An unauthorised or stale client can drive endpoints that were never associated with its stream.

requirements.title: In HW_UNCONFIGURED only the discovery claimant's stream may configure the server
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not restrict HW_UNCONFIGURED configuration requests to the discovery claimant's stream (TC18 §12.3.1.1). rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() admits any NTSCF/ACF_ABB request addressed to RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID regardless of which stream_id it arrived on, and never consults rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant(). Any client on the network can therefore configure a server that a different client is in the middle of discovering and configuring.

requirements.title: Write requests are accepted only from unicast frames
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not restrict write requests to unicast frames (TC18 §12.3.1.1, §12.3.1.2, §12.3.1.3 -- stated once for each lifecycle state). Neither rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() nor rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() is told whether the frame arrived at a unicast or a multicast/broadcast destination MAC, so a write carried in a multicast or broadcast frame is processed exactly like a unicast one. A single broadcast write frame can therefore reconfigure every RC Server on the network at once.

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED drops TSCF-headed AVTPDUs regardless of time-sync support
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP accepts TSCF-headed AVTPDUs in HW_CONFIGURED whenever the node advertises time-sync support (TC18 §12.3.1.2). The specification states that in HW_CONFIGURED, TSCF-headed AVTPDUs are dropped without further response, unconditionally -- the same rule already implemented for HW_UNCONFIGURED at src/lifecycle.c:132. A time-sync-capable server therefore processes timed requests before its RCP configuration (stream/byte_bus_id mapping, response queues) exists.

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED drops ACF_GBB-format requests without response
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not drop ACF_GBB-format requests in HW_CONFIGURED (TC18 §12.3.1.2). rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() only inspects acf_msg_type in its HW_UNCONFIGURED branch; in HW_CONFIGURED any ACF message type, including RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB, is admitted. Group-byte-bus requests are therefore processed in a state whose stream/byte_bus_id mapping is not yet validated.

requirements.title: In HW_CONFIGURED, EP0 write access to another endpoint's configuration requires the root client or the discovery stream
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP grants unrestricted functional-configuration write access in HW_CONFIGURED (TC18 §12.3.1.2). rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() returns true for RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W in HW_CONFIGURED for every rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t, whereas the specification permits cross-endpoint write access via EP0 only for a configured root client or via the discovery stream. Any client with a configured stream can reconfigure endpoints it does not own while the server is in HW_CONFIGURED.

requirements.title: A lifecycle-state write is accepted only from the discovery stream, the root client, or (with no root client) any valid stream
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not authorize the writer of a lifecycle-state change (TC18 §12.3.1.2). rcp_lifecycle_transition() accepts no rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t, and rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t itself carries no via_discovery_stream flag, so the rule that a svr_lifecycle_state write must arrive via the discovery stream, or from the configured root client, or (only when no root client is configured) from any valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination, cannot be expressed or enforced. Any client that can reach the server can promote or demote its lifecycle state.

requirements.title: In HW_CONFIGURED, non-configuration requests to endpoints other than EP0 are dropped
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not restrict HW_CONFIGURED traffic to configuration requests (TC18 §12.3.1.2). rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() admits every non-TSCF frame in HW_CONFIGURED and rcp_server_endpoint_admit()/rcp_server_endpoint_submit() have no lifecycle input, so an operational request addressed to an endpoint other than EP0 is executed or queued before the server has reached RCP_CONFIGURED, instead of being ignored and dropped without response. Endpoints can be driven before their RCP configuration has been validated.

requirements.title: Non-STANDARD requests to EP0 before full configuration must be answered with REQUEST_REJECTED, not dropped
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): while the RC Server is HW_UNCONFIGURED, or while no valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination has been defined, c-RCP admits only an NTSCF-framed ACF_ABB addressed to RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID (rcp_lifecycle_should_accept(), src/lifecycle.c:119) and silently drops every other frame. TC18 §12.7 requires instead that only unconditional STANDARD requests be accepted at EP0 in this condition and that every OTHER otherwise-valid request to EP0 be answered with an error response carrying error code REQUEST_REJECTED. c-RCP never emits RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_REJECTED anywhere, and rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() has no request-kind (RCP_SCHED_KIND_*) input with which to distinguish a STANDARD request from a compound/wait, triggered, chained or timed one. A conforming client that probes EP0 with a conditional request therefore receives silence instead of the specified diagnostic error response.

requirements.title: A direct-to-EP configuration request without a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id association must be dropped
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not drop a configuration request addressed directly to an endpoint when the endpoint has no valid stream_id/byte_bus_id association. rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() (src/lifecycle.c:119) accepts any byte_bus_id unconditionally in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED and RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED, and consults no request-stream configuration at all (its only stream evidence, rcp_lifecycle_request_stream_plausibility_t, is used solely by the transition guards). TC18 §12.7 requires that direct-to-EP configuration requests be permitted only in RCP_CONFIGURED, or in HW_CONFIGURED with a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id configuration, and dropped otherwise. Consequence: a client on an unregistered stream can reach an endpoint's configuration in HW_CONFIGURED.

requirements.title: In HW_UNCONFIGURED only the claimed discovery stream may configure the server
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): c-RCP models the discovery-stream claim (rcp_discovery_claim_note_request()/rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant(), src/discovery.c:387/399) but no code path binds it to the HW_UNCONFIGURED state as TC18 §12.7.2 requires. rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() (src/lifecycle.c:119) admits a frame in HW_UNCONFIGURED on the strength of its byte_bus_id alone, never comparing the frame's stream_id against the current discovery claimant, and rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() is a pure query no accept/reject path calls. Consequence: while HW_UNCONFIGURED, a configuration write arriving on any stream is accepted, not only one on the discovery stream assigned in answer to a discovery request.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.2 Configuration in HW_UNCONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2488-2489

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED configuration access is restricted to the discovery stream or a known stream_id/byte_bus_id pair
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED c-RCP places no restriction whatever on who may perform a configuration access — rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() returns true for RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W and RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR for every rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t, and rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() accepts every byte_bus_id. TC18 §12.7.3 permits configuration access in this state only (a) via a discovery request on the discovery stream, or (b) via a KNOWN stream_id/byte_bus_id combination addressed directly to the endpoint. Consequence: any stream may reconfigure any endpoint while the server is HW_CONFIGURED.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.3 Configuration in HW_CONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2493-2494

requirements.title: Once RCP_CONFIGURED, a discovery request may no longer change configuration although it is still answered
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): c-RCP answers discovery requests in every lifecycle state as TC18 §12.7.4 requires, but does not disable the discovery stream's configuration-write authority once RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED is reached. rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write() (src/discovery.c:409) takes only (claim, writer, now_ms) — no lifecycle state — so it will still refresh and confirm a discovery claimant's write authorization in RCP_CONFIGURED, and rcp_discovery_claim_release() is never called on the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED transition (src/lifecycle.c rcp_lifecycle_transition() touches no discovery claim). Consequence: a client holding the discovery claim retains configuration authority into RCP_CONFIGURED, where the specification grants configuration access only to a configured stream_id/byte_bus_id combination or the root client.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.4 Configuration in RCP_CONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2498-2500

requirements.title: PWM_OUT trigger events are derived from the skew-delayed signal and fire at 0% duty
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP enumerates the three TC18 Table 42 PWM_OUT trigger events (rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_t: DONE, CYCLE_START, MID_PULSE) and carries the pwmo_skew register, but implements neither of the two rules governing them -- that trigger signals are generated from the SKEW-DELAYED output rather than the undelayed one (TC18 13.7.5.1, the break-before-make provision for half/full-bridge drivers), and that the mid-active-pulse trigger fires even when the duty cycle is 0%.

requirements.title: PWM_OUT duty-cycle limits cap the requested active time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP stores pwmo_duty_cycle_min (0x000A) and pwmo_duty_cycle_max (0x000C) in rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_t but applies neither -- TC18 Table 43 requires a request whose active time falls below the minimum or exceeds the maximum to be CAPPED to that limit (not rejected, and not applied verbatim). rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() computes the new (period, active_duration) pair without consulting either register.

requirements.title: PWM_OUT request semantics: stop on period 0, output-off on active 0, phase shift, readback check
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP applies none of TC18 13.7.5.3's four PWM_OUT request rules -- a request with PWM_Period == 0 shall stop signal generation; a request with PWM_active == 0 and PWM_Period > 0 shall keep the endpoint running with the output disabled while still generating trigger signals; a request that is a trigger configuration shall have its first two payload octets read as a PHASE SHIFT rather than a period (for fixed-phase synchronisation to another PWM_OUT endpoint); and during generation the output pin shall be read back and an error signaled if it does not actually toggle. rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() stores both fields verbatim.

requirements.title: PWM_IN functional-config register block (Table 45)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_t models only the shared EP prefix plus a trigger selector, so none of TC18 Table 45's PWM_IN registers exists -- pwmi_polarity (active-phase level), pwmi_err_on_max_period (invalidate-and-rearm vs stop-and-error when MAX_PERIOD is exceeded), pwmi_continuous_mode (one-shot with a deferred response vs continuous with an immediate last-result response), pwmi_max_period, pwmi_base_clk, pwmi_clk_divider and pwmi_ep_status. The measurement-timeout sentinel RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL is the only related surface.

requirements.title: A cold start restores the configured lifecycle state, not always HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not restore the RC Server's configured lifecycle state after a cold start (TC18 §12.3, §12.4.1). rcp_pwrmode_cold_start_lifecycle_target() always returns RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED, whereas the specification requires the server to come up in the lifecycle state it is actually configured in -- recovered from NVM where present, or from device defaults which may themselves be an advanced state. A server that had reached RCP_CONFIGURED therefore silently loses its configuration on every power cycle and must be re-discovered and re-configured.

requirements.title: Configuration data and wake sources survive StandBy
requirements.text: An RC Server entering RCP_PWRMODE_STANDBY shall retain its register-map configuration (rcp_regmap_general_t, every endpoint's generic and functional configuration, request-stream and response-queue configuration) and its configured wake-up sources (rcp_ep_wakeup_functional_cfg_t.sources), such that a subsequent hot start reported as RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT requires no reconfiguration; only a transition classified RCP_PWRMODE_START_COLD may discard configuration.

requirements.title: Hot start checks network availability before sending a WakeUp
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the network-availability check in the hot-start sequence (TC18 §12.4.1). rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled() advances the handshake to RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_IFACE_REENABLED without any network-available input, and rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() is then driven regardless, whereas the specification requires the server to enable the interface, test whether the network is available, and only initiate a network WakeUp when it is not. A server can burn its whole WakeUp repeat budget against a link that is already up, or transmit into a link that is not.

requirements.title: The wake response is sent on the responder stream configured for the original sleep/standby request
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not record or use the responder stream of the original sleep/standby request when waking (TC18 §12.4.1). The pending-request state kept by rcp_powerstate_manager_encode_entry_request() holds only the target mode and transaction number, and rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() has no stream identity, so nothing constrains the repetitive wake response to travel back on the responder stream that carried the sleep request. The client that put the server to sleep may never see the wake response.

requirements.title: WakeUp repetition stops on any valid AVTPDU from the sleep-request client
requirements.text: c-RCP's WakeUp repetition termination condition diverges from TC18 §12.4.1: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() stops only when rcp_ep_wakeup_is_wakeup_echo() matched an exact echo of the WakeUp message it sent, or when hs->wakeup_repeat_limit is exhausted, whereas the specification stops repetition on receipt of ANY valid AVTPDU from the sleep-request client and defines no repeat limit. The requirement shall record that the handshake terminates on any valid AVTPDU from that client, and that the repeat limit is an implementation-added safety bound whose exhaustion degrades to RCP_PWRMODE_START_COLD.

requirements.title: Completing the wake handshake re-enables every used endpoint and response queue
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's wake handshake does not actually re-enable anything (TC18 §12.4.1). rcp_pwrmode_handshake_resume_queues() advances only a state enum to RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_COMPLETE; it does not set ep_enable on every used endpoint (rcp_server_endpoint_set_enable()), does not resume the response queues, and does not restart heartbeat-configured response streams. A woken server therefore reports a completed hot start while its endpoints remain disabled and its clients see no heartbeat.

requirements.title: A network wake skips only the interface-enable step, not the rest of the hot-start sequence
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP skips the entire hot-start handshake for a network wake (TC18 §12.4.1). rcp_pwrmode_hotstart_required() returns false for RCP_PWRMODE_WAKE_VIA_NETWORK, so rcp_pwrmode_wake_from_sleep() declares a hot start immediately, whereas the specification requires a TC14/TC10-network-woken server to skip only the interface-enable step and then proceed exactly as a pin/EP wake does: check network availability, send the repetitive wake response to the sleep-request client, and re-enable endpoints and queues on its reply. A network-woken server therefore never tells the sleeping client it is awake.

requirements.title: StandBy is entered only in response to an RCP request, never from a network signal
requirements.text: An RC Server built on c-RCP shall enter RCP_PWRMODE_STANDBY only as the result of a SleepCMD request addressed to its wake-up endpoint (rcp_ep_wakeup_decode_sleepcmd_request() reporting target mode RCP_PWRMODE_STANDBY); no network-level signal, including a TC14/TC10 sleep request, shall cause a transition into RCP_PWRMODE_STANDBY. rcp_pwrmode_transition() shall not be driven to RCP_PWRMODE_STANDBY from any network-triggered path.

requirements.title: Sleep can also be initiated by a valid network TC14/TC10 sleep request
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP has no network-initiated sleep path (TC18 §12.5). The only way to enter RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP is a SleepCMD request decoded by rcp_ep_wakeup_decode_sleepcmd_request(); nothing accepts a TC14/TC10 network sleep request, so a c-RCP server ignores the network-wide sleep coordination the rest of the vehicle uses. The server stays awake when the network is put to sleep, defeating the network's own power management.

requirements.title: A sleep/standby request from an authorized client applies to the entire RC Server
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP treats a sleep/standby request as a per-endpoint operation and applies no authorization to it (TC18 §12.5). rcp_powerstate_manager_encode_entry_request()/_apply_entry_response() track and mutate the power mode of one addressed endpoint, whereas the specification says an accepted request puts the entire RC Server implementation into standby or sleep; and nothing checks that the requesting client is one allowed to access the RC Server's wake-up endpoint. An unauthorized client can address the wake-up endpoint, and an authorized one cannot express a whole-server sleep.

requirements.title: A wake-source event during sleep-request processing aborts the sleep entry
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not abort a sleep entry on a wake-source event that arrives while the request is being processed (TC18 §12.5). rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() evaluates its gate once, at the start, and nothing re-checks rcp_ep_wakeup_any_source_asserted()/rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_is_clear() before the mode actually changes, so a wake event racing the sleep request is lost and the server sleeps through the very condition that should have kept it awake. This is a lost-wakeup hazard, not merely a missed optimization.

requirements.title: The sleep/standby refusal conditions are evaluated server-wide, across every EP and every responder queue
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's sleep/standby entry gate is scoped to a single endpoint and a single queue (TC18 §12.5). rcp_pwrmode_entry_gate_t.endpoint_idle is documented as the wake-up endpoint's own idleness and response_queue_empty as one queue's emptiness, whereas the specification refuses entry when AT LEAST ONE endpoint of the whole server is not idle or AT LEAST ONE responder queue still holds a message pending transmission. A server can therefore be put to sleep with other endpoints mid-request and undelivered responses still queued, losing both.

requirements.title: The mode change happens only after the sleep/standby response has been transmitted
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP imposes no ordering between emitting the sleep/standby response and performing the mode transition (TC18 §12.5). rcp_ep_wakeup_encode_sleepcmd_response() and rcp_pwrmode_transition() are unrelated calls, so a caller may legitimately change mode before the response has left the interface. Entering Sleep before the response is transmitted loses the acknowledgement the client needs to know the server complied, and can strand the client waiting on a server that is already powered down.

requirements.title: A refused network sleep request suppresses the TC14/TC10 LPS confirmation
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model TC14/TC10 LPS confirmation (TC18 §12.5). There is no network sleep-request path and no PHY-signalling surface, so the requirement that the PHY must NOT signal LPS when rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() would refuse the entry cannot be honoured or tested. On a real device this is the only way an upstream node learns the server declined to sleep, so the network can proceed to sleep while this node stays awake.

requirements.title: Sleep-request processing order: stop admitting requests, drain, then acknowledge
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP evaluates TC18 13.7.2.3's step-3 preconditions (rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() requires wup_status clear, all endpoints idle and every responder queue empty) but does not implement step 1 -- on receipt of a sleep request the server shall stop entering newly arriving requests into endpoint queues while the drain proceeds. The library exposes no admission-suspend state, so a request arriving mid-drain is admitted normally.

requirements.title: The lifecycle state is exposed as the svr_lifecycle_state register-map entry
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not expose the lifecycle state as a register-map entry (TC18 §12.3.1.1, §12.3.1.2, §12.4.1). rcp_regmap_general_t has no svr_lifecycle_state field, so a client can neither read the server's current lifecycle state (required after a cold start to decide whether further configuration is needed) nor drive a transition by writing it -- the only entry point is the in-process rcp_lifecycle_transition() call. Discovery of a server's readiness over the wire is therefore impossible.

requirements.title: The RC Server general register map is only reachable on the wire for its first 14 octets
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): c-RCP exposes the RC Server general register map over ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB only through the discovery read response, which encodes exclusively the leading RCP_DISCOVERY_GENERAL_SLICE_LEN (14) octets at absolute addresses 0x0000..0x000D (rcp_discovery_encode_response(), src/discovery.c). No encode/decode or read/write handler exists for any other register in TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 (0x000E..0x0030 and the continued optional-subsystem pointers), so an RC Client cannot read this server's capability, capacity, lock or sub-table-pointer registers at all. rcp_regmap_general_t is an in-process model only; consequently EP0 is not a fully addressable register space as TC18 §12.7 requires.

requirements.title: Every register in the RC Server static part is read-only to a remote client
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 marks every register of the RC Server general (static) part with access type R — a remote write to any of them must not take effect. c-RCP has no read-only register class: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c) knows only RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC, _FUNCTIONAL_W and _FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR, none of which denies a write in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED, and rcp_regmap_general_t is handed out for unrestricted mutation (rcp_mock_server_regmap(), include/rcp/mock.h:174). Because no wire write path into the general register map exists at all (see the umbrella entry), the read-only property is presently unobservable rather than enforced; it must be stated and enforced when that path is added.

requirements.title: svr_req_stream_max (0x000E) is the wrong width and svr_responder_streams_max (0x000F) is missing
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_req_stream_max as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x000E (maximum number of request streams usable to access this RC Server) and svr_responder_streams_max as an 8-bit read-only register at 0x000F (maximum number of supported responder queues for response and acknowledge traffic). c-RCP declares rcp_regmap_general_t.svr_max_request_streams as a 16-bit field (include/rcp/regmap.h:208) with no address binding, and declares nothing at all for svr_responder_streams_max. Consequence: a client cannot learn either limit, and the request-stream limit cannot be represented at the specified width.

requirements.title: The two memory-capacity registers svr_responder_mem_size (0x0010) and svr_req_mem_size (0x0012) are missing
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines two distinct 16-bit read-only capacity registers, both counted in 32-bit words: svr_responder_mem_size at absolute address 0x0010 (maximum responder-queue memory) and svr_req_mem_size at 0x0012 (maximum memory for EP request queues). c-RCP models neither; rcp_regmap_general_t carries one undifferentiated 32-bit svr_memory_capacity field (include/rcp/regmap.h:210) with no address, no unit and no consumer anywhere in src/. Consequence: a client cannot size its responder queues or its per-endpoint request storage against the server's real limits, and the two limits cannot be distinguished.

requirements.title: svr_sequencers_max (0x0014) is 16-bit and its 0-means-unsupported encoding is unenforced
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_sequencers_max as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0014 whose value 0 means sequencer operation is not supported and whose values 1..n give the number of available sequencer state registers. c-RCP declares rcp_regmap_general_t.svr_max_sequencers as a 16-bit field (include/rcp/regmap.h:209) with no address binding, and no function in the tree treats 0 as "sequencer operation not supported" — request_sequencer.h merely documents the field as a runtime bound (include/rcp/request_sequencer.h:42,81). Consequence: a server that does not implement sequencers cannot advertise that fact at the specified width, and a client cannot detect it from this register.

requirements.title: svr_configuration_lock (0x0015) is entirely missing, so R/W+ writes are never lock-gated
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP has no svr_configuration_lock register. TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines it as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0015 whose value 0x00 permits write access to "R/W+" type parameters and whose every other value causes such write access to be rejected. rcp_regmap_general_t (include/rcp/regmap.h:199-222) declares no such field, and rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c) grants or denies RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR writes purely from the lifecycle state and writer context, with no lock input. Consequence: a device that has latched its configuration cannot express that latch to clients, and c-RCP will accept an R/W+ write that a conforming server would reject.

requirements.title: svr_implemented_options (0x0016) uses an invented 32-bit layout and cannot advertise trigger or chained requests
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial, and non-conforming): TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_implemented_options as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0016 with one bit per optional feature: a = compound & wait requests, b = trigger requests, c = chained requests, d = time synch and timed requests, e = enhanced request cancellation. c-RCP instead declares rcp_regmap_general_t.svr_implemented_options as a 32-bit field (include/rcp/regmap.h:211) carrying six bits of this project's own invention, grouped into three all-or-nothing PAIRS (RCP_REGMAP_OPT_TIME_SYNC_TSCF/_PRESENTATION, _ENH_CANCEL_REQUEST/_ACK, _COMPOUND_HEADER/_SEGMENT, include/rcp/regmap.h:179-188) that correspond to no spec bit position. No bit exists for trigger requests (spec bit b) or chained requests (spec bit c), even though c-RCP implements both request types (src/request_triggered.c, src/request_chained.c). Consequences: (1) the register is unreadable/uninterpretable by a conforming RC Client, since the bit positions and the field width are both wrong; (2) a c-RCP server cannot advertise trigger or chained request support at all, so a conforming client must assume it has neither; (3) rcp_regmap_options_group_consistent() (src/regmap.c:20) enforces a pairing rule the specification does not have.

requirements.title: The reserved octet at 0x0017 must read 0x00
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 reserves the 8-bit register at absolute address 0x0017 and requires it to read 0x00. c-RCP models no reserved field in rcp_regmap_general_t and no absolute-address layout for the general register map, so a read of 0x0017 returns nothing defined. Consequence: forward compatibility is not preserved — a client that reads the block cannot rely on the reserved octet being zero.

requirements.title: svr_io_pin_count (0x0018) is missing, so the HW_config table has no declared extent
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP has no svr_io_pin_count register. TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines it as a 16-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0018 giving the number of assignable I/O pins, and §12.7.6 makes it the authoritative source for how many IO-pin entries the HW_config table (Table 19) contains. rcp_regmap_general_t declares no such field. Consequence: neither a client nor c-RCP itself can bound the HW_config table, so a write addressed past the last real IO pin has no defined limit to be checked against.

requirements.title: svr_hw_cfg_ptr (0x001A) is modeled as a 32-bit word-unit offset with a spurious capacity
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_hw_cfg_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer register at absolute address 0x001A, giving the address of the HW_config register map of §12.7.6. c-RCP represents it as rcp_regmap_general_t.hw_pin_map, an rcp_regmap_table_ref_t whose offset member is a 32-bit value expressed in this implementation's own "register words" (include/rcp/regmap.h:167-173) rather than a 16-bit register-map address, and which carries an extra capacity member that TC18 does not define for this table (HW_config's extent is svr_io_pin_count at 0x0018). Consequence: the pointer cannot be encoded into its 16-bit register slot without a unit conversion c-RCP does not define, and the capacity member invites a second, contradictory source of truth for the table's length.

requirements.title: The request/response stream config pointer and capacity registers have the wrong widths and no addresses
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines four separate registers for the stream-configuration sub-tables — svr_request_stream_cfg_capacity (8 bit, 0x001C), svr_response_stream_cfg_capacity (8 bit, 0x001D), svr_request_stream_cfg_ptr (16 bit, 0x001E) and svr_response_stream_cfg_ptr (16 bit, 0x0020). c-RCP collapses each pointer/capacity pair into one rcp_regmap_table_ref_t (include/rcp/regmap.h:216-217) with a 32-bit word-unit offset and a 16-bit capacity, binds none of the four to its absolute address, and encodes none of them on the wire. Consequence: an RC Client cannot discover how many request streams / response-and-acknowledge streams this server will accept, nor where either configuration table lives.

requirements.title: The reserved 16-bit register at 0x0022 must be preserved as reserved
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 reserves the 16-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0022. c-RCP models no reserved field in rcp_regmap_general_t and has no absolute-address layout for the general register map, so a read of 0x0022 returns nothing defined and the address is free to be reused by mistake. Consequence: forward compatibility with a future TC18 revision that assigns this register is not preserved.

requirements.title: svr_ep_generic_cfg_capacity (0x0026) is a byte length, but c-RCP models capacity as an entry count
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial, semantically contradictory): TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at absolute address 0x0024 to the generic endpoint register map (§13.2), and svr_ep_generic_cfg_capacity as a 16-bit read-only register at 0x0026 giving the LENGTH OF THE EP CONFIG REGISTER SECTION IN BYTES. c-RCP represents both by rcp_regmap_general_t.ep_generic_cfg, an rcp_regmap_table_ref_t whose capacity member is explicitly documented as an entry count rather than an octet length (include/rcp/regmap.h:167-169). Consequence: if the field were ever encoded into 0x0026 as-is, a conforming client would compute the section extent wrongly by a factor of sizeof(one EP config entry).

requirements.title: svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr (0x0028) / _capacity (0x002A) have the wrong widths and no addresses
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at absolute address 0x0028 to the EP-to-byte_bus_id mapping table, and svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_capacity as an 8-bit read-only register at 0x002A giving that table's maximum entry count. c-RCP folds both into rcp_regmap_general_t.ep_id_bus_map (include/rcp/regmap.h:220), an rcp_regmap_table_ref_t with a 32-bit word-unit offset and a 16-bit capacity, bound to no address and encoded nowhere. Consequence: a client cannot locate or size the mapping table that tells it which byte_bus_id reaches which endpoint — the very table it needs before it may address an endpoint directly (§12.7).

requirements.title: svr_ep_functional_cfg_ptr (0x002C) and svr_sequencer_state_ptr (0x002E) are 32-bit word offsets with no addresses
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_ep_functional_cfg_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at absolute address 0x002C to the EP_FUNC_config register map, and svr_sequencer_state_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at 0x002E to the sequencer state registers (§12.7.10). c-RCP represents both as rcp_regmap_table_ref_t members (include/rcp/regmap.h:219,221) carrying a 32-bit offset in this implementation's own register-word units plus a capacity member the specification does not define for either pointer, none of it bound to an address or encoded on the wire. Consequence: a client cannot locate the endpoint functional-configuration section — the section §12.7.1's configuration request exists to write — nor the sequencer state registers.

requirements.title: All four optional-subsystem pointer/capacity register pairs (network, physical layer, time synch, security) are missing
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18's continued part defines four further 16-bit read-only pointer/capacity register pairs in the RC Server general register map — svr_network_interface_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.11), svr_physical_layer_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.12), svr_time_synch_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.13) and svr_security_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.14) — where a pointer value of 0 is the defined encoding for "this subsystem is not supported" for the physical-layer, time-synch and security pointers. c-RCP declares none of the eight registers: rcp_regmap_general_t carries only seven sub-table references (include/rcp/regmap.h:215-221) and none corresponds to these subsystems. Consequence: a c-RCP server cannot advertise, and a c-RCP client cannot discover, whether network-interface, physical-layer, time-synchronisation or security configuration is present — including the "not supported" answer, which the specification requires be expressible as a zero pointer.

requirements.title: No HW_config table exists to hold per-IO-pin endpoint-signal assignments
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP has no HW_config register map. TC18 §12.7.6 requires a table holding, for each used physical IO-pin, its mapping to an endpoint signal and its IO-pin properties, defaulting at the factory to no assignment at all. c-RCP defines the shape of a single row (rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_entry_t, include/rcp/regmap.h:300-304) and a pointer/capacity descriptor for the table (rcp_regmap_general_t.hw_pin_map), but no array, no server-side storage, and no write path: rcp_config_apply_to_mock() deliberately discards the parsed hw_pin_map (include/rcp/config.h:149-155). Consequence: endpoint signals can never actually be bound to physical IO pins, so the HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT guard's hw_pin_mapped input (src/lifecycle.c:33) is supplied entirely by the caller with nothing in the library backing it.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 HW pin mapping configuration, TC18.txt L2691-2695

requirements.title: HW_config rows are 3 octets per IO pin at relative addresses 3*N, 3*N+1, 3*N+2
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.6 Table 19 lays the HW_config map out as three consecutive 8-bit R/W* registers per physical IO pin — hw_ep_nr, hw_ep_pin_nr, hw_pin_type — so that IO_Pin 1 occupies relative addresses 0x0000/0x0001/0x0002, IO_Pin 2 occupies 0x0003/0x0004/0x0005, IO_Pin 3 begins at 0x0006, and IO pin N begins at relative address 3*N. c-RCP declares the three fields as rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_entry_t (include/rcp/regmap.h:300-304, third field spelled pin_property rather than hw_pin_type) but defines no relative addressing, no 3-octet stride, and no encode/decode pair, and provides no setter that routes the write through rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() with RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC to enforce the R/W* (HW_unconfigured-only) access type. Consequence: the HW_config table cannot be read or written over the wire at the specified layout, and its HW_unconfigured-only writability is unenforced for the actual pin entries.

requirements.title: hw_pin_type bit layout contradicts Table 20 and omits open-source, drive strength and Schmitt-trigger
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (non-conforming): TC18 §12.7.6 Table 20 defines the hw_pin_type octet as four packed sub-fields — Pull-Up at bits 1:0 (00b float, 01b pull down, 10b pull up), Output stage at bits 3:2 (00b input, 01b open drain, 10b open source, 11b push pull), Drive strength at bits 5:4 (00b input, 01b low, 10b medium, 11b high), reserved bit 6 reading 0, and Schmitt-Trigger enable at bit 7. c-RCP instead defines six independent one-hot flags of its own invention (RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_OUTPUT/_INPUT/_OPEN_DRAIN/_PULL_UP/_PULL_DOWN/_ACTIVE_LOW, include/rcp/regmap.h:293-298), which occupy different bit positions, cannot express open source, any of the three drive strengths, the Schmitt-trigger selection, or the explicit float encoding, and add an ACTIVE_LOW property TC18 does not define. Consequence: a c-RCP-written hw_pin_type octet configures the wrong pin electrical properties on a conforming RC PHY — e.g. c-RCP's PULL_UP (bit 3) lands in the Output-stage field and reads as open drain.

requirements.title: An output pin is always simultaneously an input
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (contradicted): TC18 §12.7.6 states that the pin direction/drive entry is split into exactly four sub-fields (pull resistor, output stage, drive strength, Schmitt-trigger) and that ALL OUTPUTS ARE ALWAYS ALSO AN INPUT — output and input are not mutually exclusive pin states. c-RCP models RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_OUTPUT and RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_INPUT as two separate flags and rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_gpio.c:98) toggles a pin from one to the other, so a pin configured as an output ceases to be readable as an input. Consequence: read-back of an output pin's actual level — the standard way to detect a short or a stuck driver — is not expressible, and the four-section decomposition Table 20 mandates is absent.

requirements.title: The EP_Signal_Nr enumeration covers only GPIO, SPI and I2C
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): TC18 §12.7.6 Table 21 enumerates the EP_Signal_Nr values for every endpoint type — GPIO 0..31; SPI 0..8 (CLK, PICO, POCI, CS0..CS5); I2C 0..1 (SCL, SDA); UART 0..3 (TX, RX, RTS, CTS); LIN 0..2 (TXD, RXD, NSLP); PWM_OUT 0..1 (positive phase, inverted phase); PWM_IN 0; ADC 0 (ADC_IN); DAC 0 (DAC_OUT); CAN 0 RXD and 1 TXD; ISELED 0 ISP_P and 1 ISP_N; MDIO 0 MDC and 1 MDIO. c-RCP's rcp_regmap_named_signal_t (include/rcp/regmap.h:311-357) enumerates only GPIO, SPI and I2C, ending at RCP_REGMAP_SIGNAL_I2C_SDA. Consequence: the hw_ep_pin_nr value of a HW_config entry cannot be named or validated for the seven other endpoint types c-RCP implements, and CAN's counter-intuitive ordering (RXD = 0, TXD = 1) is nowhere recorded, inviting a transposed pin map.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21: Enumeration of signals at endpoints, TC18.txt L2779-2820

requirements.title: EP_Signal_Nr restarts at 0 for each endpoint type, but c-RCP numbers signals globally
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (contradicted): TC18 §12.7.6 states the EP_Pin_Nr mapping is specific per endpoint type, and Table 21 accordingly restarts EP_Signal_Nr at 0 for every EP_Type — SPI_CLK is 0, I2C_SCL is 0, UART_TX is 0, CAN RXD is 0, and so on — so that hw_ep_pin_nr in a HW_config entry (Table 19, relative address 0x0001) is interpreted relative to the endpoint type named by hw_ep_nr. c-RCP's rcp_regmap_named_signal_t (include/rcp/regmap.h:311-357) is instead one flat global enumeration in which SPI_CLK is 32 and I2C_SCL is 41, and no function converts a global index to a per-type EP_Signal_Nr or back. Consequence: if a c-RCP value were written into hw_ep_pin_nr, a conforming RC PHY would bind the wrong endpoint signal — c-RCP's SPI_CLK (32) exceeds the SPI type's whole 0..8 signal range.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21 + Table 19 row hw_ep_pin_nr, TC18.txt L2704, L2764, L2779-2820

requirements.title: the four product-specific configuration-section pointer/capacity pairs in the general register map
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: rcp_regmap_general_t declares no pointer/capacity pairs for the four product-specific configuration sections TC18 defines: svr_network_interface_cfg_ptr/svr_network_interface_cfg_capacity (§12.7.11, the entire MAC configuration for an Ethernet interface), svr_physical_layer_cfg_ptr/svr_physical_layer_cfg_capacity (§12.7.12, which may be empty for MDIO Manageable Devices reachable through an MDIO endpoint instead), svr_time_synch_cfg_ptr/svr_timesynch_cfg_capacity (§12.7.13, typically gPTP per IEEE 802.1AS), and svr_security_cfg_ptr/svr_security_cfg_capacity (§12.7.14, typically MACsec per IEEE 802.1AE and its key agreement). Each section shall start at its pointer register and span to pointer + capacity. Consequence: four of the eleven sub-tables a conforming general register map advertises are absent, so a client discovering a c-RCP server cannot locate its MAC, PHY, time-sync or security configuration, and cannot tell that a section is empty (capacity 0) as opposed to unadvertised.

requirements.title: Request-stream config carries a per-stream secure-channel index selecting the MACsec channel
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the per-request-stream rx_secure_channel_index register (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000C, 8 bit, R/W*). rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t has no secure-channel member, so a server built on this library cannot select which secure channel a request stream is carried on, and cannot express the default value 0 meaning "no cyber security, MACsec uncontrolled port". Consequence: every request stream is implicitly on the uncontrolled port; a client that configures a protected channel per stream has no register to write and the server silently accepts traffic it should have required MACsec protection on.

requirements.title: request stream's acknowledge-stream pointer (rx_ack_stream_index)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model rx_ack_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x0010, 8 bit, R/W*), the index of the stream on which endpoints bound to this request stream shall send their acknowledges, with the value 0 meaning "no acknowledge is to be sent". rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t carries no such field and no code path routes an acknowledgement to a selected response queue. Consequence: acknowledgements cannot be directed to (or suppressed on) a per-request-stream basis, and the "0 = no ack" suppression the specification defines cannot be configured at all.

requirements.title: request stream's response-stream pointer and its discovery-enabling default of 1 (rx_resp_stream_index)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model rx_resp_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x0011, 8 bit, R/W*), the index of the stream on which endpoints bound to this request stream shall send their responses, with 0 meaning "no response is to be sent" and a power-on default of 1 so that a discovery request can be answered before any configuration has been written. rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t carries no such field; rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() only checks a boolean has_response_stream (src/lifecycle.c:59), which records that some response stream exists but not which one, and rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_init() zeroes every field rather than defaulting this one to 1. Consequence: responses cannot be routed per request stream, response suppression cannot be configured, and the specification's own bootstrap guarantee (a freshly reset server can answer discovery because index 1 is preselected) is not reproduced.

requirements.title: Watchdog timeout register width and unit deviate from Table 22's 16-bit clock-tick field
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t.rx_wd_timeout_ms shall represent TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22's rx_wd_timeout_intervall register (relative address 0x000A, 16 bit, R/W*, expressed in clock tics). c-RCP deliberately stores it as a 32-bit millisecond value and rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() compares it against elapsed_since_last_kick_ms, so a conversion between the server's clock-tick domain and milliseconds shall be applied at the register-write boundary, and a written value shall be rejected if it does not fit the register's 16-bit width. NOT IMPLEMENTED: no such conversion or width check exists. Consequence: a client writing the register in clock tics and a server reading it as milliseconds disagree about the watchdog period by the tick rate, and values above 0xFFFF are silently accepted for a register that cannot hold them.

requirements.title: Table 22's W* fields are writable in both HW_UNCONFIGURED and HW_CONFIGURED and read-only in RCP_CONFIGURED
