requirements.text: Every field of the request-stream configuration table (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22) marked R/W* shall be classified RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR and shall be writable while the server is in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED or RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED and read-only in RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED. c-RCP deviates on both halves: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c:170) denies FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR writes in HW_UNCONFIGURED, and no register-map write path in the codebase classifies the request-stream table as FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR at all, so the RCP_CONFIGURED lock is never actually applied to Table 22.

requirements.title: EP_ID_config rows are (Request_Stream_Index, EP_Nr, BBID) triples, not (EP_Nr, BBID) pairs
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t shall model one full row of the EP_ID_config table (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23): a Request_Stream_Index (relative offset 0x0000 within the row, 8 bit, R/W+), an EP_Nr (0x0001, 8 bit, R/W+) and a BBID (0x0002, 16 bit, R/W+), so that the same byte_bus_id can be mapped to different endpoints on different request streams. NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's entry type omits Request_Stream_Index entirely (include/rcp/regmap.h:458-461), reducing the table to a global byte_bus_id → ep_id map. Consequence: the specification's central addressing rule — that a byte_bus_id is unique only within the stream_id it is paired with (as include/rcp/avtp.h:124-127 itself states) — cannot be represented, so two RC Clients on different streams cannot legally reuse a byte_bus_id, and the per-stream mapping §12.9.1's lookup depends on does not exist.

requirements.title: byte_bus_id is an 11-bit address; the 8-bit rcp_byte_bus_id_t cannot represent addresses 256..2047
requirements.text: rcp_byte_bus_id_t shall be wide enough to hold the full 11-bit byte_bus_id the EP_ID_config table's BBID register carries (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23, row offset 0x0002, 16 bit register, "Byte_bus_id [11bit]") and that the ACF byte_message_info header transports across octet 2 bits [2:0] and octet 3 (REQ-ACF-016). NOT IMPLEMENTED: rcp_byte_bus_id_t is uint8_t (include/rcp/avtp.h:127), so byte_bus_id[10:8] is structurally always zero on encode (src/acf.c:65) and cannot be recovered on decode. Consequence: c-RCP can address only 256 of the 2048 endpoints per stream the protocol defines, and REQ-ACF-016's header-layout obligation is unsatisfiable for any address above 255 — a peer legitimately using BBID 0x100..0x7FF is unaddressable and its frames are mis-decoded to the low 8 bits.

requirements.title: A Request_Stream_Index of 0 terminates the EP_ID_config table, and the power-on defaults address EP0
requirements.text: Every consumer of the EP_ID_config table shall stop scanning at the first row whose Request_Stream_Index is 0, that value denoting the end of the table rather than a valid stream index (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23 / L2976), and the table's power-on default contents (Request_Stream_Index = 1, EP_Nr = 0, BBID = 0) shall permit access to EP0 before any configuration is written. NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's ep-id map carries no Request_Stream_Index at all and is delimited by an explicit caller-supplied count, so neither the sentinel nor the EP0-reachable default state is expressible. Consequence: a table image received from a conforming client cannot be interpreted — trailing zero rows are read as real mappings to EP0/BBID 0.

requirements.title: the W+ lockable access type for EP_ID_config and the Table 24 W+ queue fields
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP models no W+ (explicitly lockable) register access type. TC18 marks every EP_ID_config row R/W+ (§12.7.8 Table 23) and the STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time queue registers R/W+ (§12.7.9 Table 24); W+ means the table may be locked by the configuring instance to protect against unwanted later modification, independently of the lifecycle state that governs W and W*. rcp_lifecycle_field_kind_t (include/rcp/lifecycle.h:227-229) defines only HW_GENERIC, FUNCTIONAL_W and FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR, and rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() takes no lock state. Consequence: a client that has finished configuring the endpoint map has no way to latch it, so a later erroneous or malicious write can silently re-point byte_bus_ids at different endpoints while the server remains in a state that permits W+ writes.

requirements.title: EP_ID_config ordering is ascending in (Request_Stream_Index, BBID), not BBID alone
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_ascending() shall report whether the EP_ID_config table is ordered ascending in the composite key (Request_Stream_Index, BBID), the ordering TC18 §12.7.8 requires the configuring instance to maintain and whose violation the specification says can cause requests to be dropped because no endpoint is found. c-RCP's implementation checks only strictly increasing byte_bus_id and is structurally unable to consider Request_Stream_Index (include/rcp/regmap.h:458-461, 469). Consequence: a table that is correctly ordered per-stream but interleaves streams is reported non-ascending, and a table that is ascending in BBID but scrambled across streams is reported ascending — the diagnostic gives the wrong answer in both directions once more than one request stream is configured.

requirements.title: single-RC-Client-per-endpoint recommendation is neither enforced nor diagnosed
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP provides no check that an endpoint is mapped to at most one RC Client at a time, the arrangement TC18 §12.7.8 recommends for safety reasons. rcp_regmap_ep_client_t.owning_stream_index (include/rcp/regmap.h:236-239) exists solely to authorize functional-config writes (REQ-RMAP-011/012) and does not constrain which request streams may deliver requests to the endpoint, and no diagnostic analogous to rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_ascending() reports the multi-client condition. Consequence: two RC Clients can concurrently drive the same actuator endpoint with no warning, which is precisely the hazard the recommendation exists to prevent.

requirements.title: endpoints sharing a byte_bus_id within one stream should be of the same ep_type
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not check that all endpoints mapped to the same byte_bus_id within a single request stream share an ep_type, as TC18 §12.7.8 recommends. A shared byte_bus_id is a deliberate multicast-within-a-stream mechanism, and a request broadcast to endpoints of differing ep_type is decoded differently by each. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t (include/rcp/regmap.h:458-461) carries no ep_type and nothing cross-references rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_t.ep_type. Consequence: one write request can be interpreted as, say, a GPIO bitmask by one endpoint and a PWM duty value by another, with no configuration-time diagnostic.

requirements.title: per-response/acknowledge-stream transmit queue and its queue_size register
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP reserves no transmit queue per response or acknowledge stream, and models no queue_size register (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0004, 16 bit, R/W*, "Queue N assigned memory in 32bit words"). rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t (include/rcp/regmap.h:447-451) carries three configuration values with no storage behind them, and the only queue in the codebase is server.h's inbound per-endpoint ep_enable pre-load queue, which holds requests, not responses. Consequence: responses and acknowledges from endpoints and from the RC Server itself are never collected for aggregated transmission, so none of §12.7.9's flush/heartbeat/AVTPDU-packing behavior can exist and the memory the specification requires the server to reserve is unaccounted for.

requirements.title: response queue's STREAM_UID (the unique_id half of the queue's outgoing stream_id)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the STREAM_UID register (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0000, 16 bit, R/W+), which supplies bits [63:48] of the stream_id a response queue transmits on — the unique_id half of the MAC-plus-unique_id stream_id rcp_stream_id_make() (include/rcp/avtp.h:130) already builds. rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t carries no such field. Consequence: a response queue has no identity, responses cannot be addressed to a specific outgoing stream, and rx_ack_stream_index/rx_resp_stream_index (Table 22) have nothing to point at.

requirements.title: Max_AVTPDUsize bounds every transmitted AVTPDU, is MTU-consistent, and is discoverable
requirements.text: The RC Server shall not transmit an AVTPDU longer than the configured Max_AVTPDUsize (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0002, 16 bit, R/W*, expressed in quadlets), shall reject a configured value for which the resulting network frame would exceed the network's maximum transmit unit, and shall expose the value in the Info/Config register map so a peer can discover it. c-RCP implements only the register field (include/rcp/regmap.h:448): no transmit path bounds a frame by it, no MTU consistency check exists, and it is not part of the discovery general-register slice (include/rcp/discovery.h:212, RCP_DISCOVERY_GENERAL_SLICE_LEN == 14 octets). Consequence: the server can emit AVTPDUs the link will drop, and a client cannot discover the server's own frame ceiling.

requirements.title: A single ACF message exceeding Max_AVTPDUsize is fragmented via the ms bit
requirements.text: When a single ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB message queued for transmission would produce an AVTPDU exceeding the response queue's configured Max_AVTPDUsize, the RC Server shall fragment it using the ms-bit/segment_num mechanism fragment.h implements, calling rcp_fragment_plan() with max_fragment_payload derived from rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.max_avtpdu_size (TC18 §12.7.9). c-RCP implements the fragmentation mechanism itself (rcp_fragment_plan()/rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed(), REQ-FRAG-002..018) but never derives its bound from max_avtpdu_size — the only configured ceiling wired into fragment.h is the request-side rx_stream_max_request_size. Consequence: the transmit direction has no size trigger at all, so an oversized single-message response is emitted unfragmented rather than split.

requirements.title: flush_on_count triggers transmission of the whole queue packed into Max_AVTPDUsize-bounded AVTPDUs
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement the flush_on_count trigger (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0006, 16 bit, R/W+, default 1 meaning immediate transmission, legal range 1..queue_size in 32-bit-word entries). Once a response queue holds at least flush_on_count quadlets the server shall begin transmitting, packing as many ACF messages as fit within Max_AVTPDUsize into each AVTPDU and emitting as many AVTPDUs as are needed to drain every queued message including the one that crossed the threshold. rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.flush_on_count (include/rcp/regmap.h:449) is an inert field with no queue behind it and no packer to drive; scheduler.h implements only the inverse split (rcp_sched_split_frame_members(), REQ-SCHED-004). Consequence: response batching does not exist, so neither the latency/throughput trade-off the register configures nor the multi-message AVTPDU packing the protocol relies on is available.

requirements.title: Flush_time forces transmission once the configured interval since the last transmission elapses
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement the Flush_time trigger (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0008, 16 bit, R/W+, microseconds, 0 meaning "flush only by count"). The server shall initiate transmission from a response queue whenever the time since that queue's last transmission is equal to or greater than Flush_time, independently of flush_on_count. rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.flush_time_us (include/rcp/regmap.h:450) is inert; watchdog.c's Keeper is the codebase's only periodic timer and it evaluates watchdogs, not queues. Consequence: a queue holding fewer than flush_on_count quadlets is never drained, so low-rate responses are held indefinitely.

requirements.title: an empty response queue still emits a heartbeat AVTPDU on Flush_time expiry
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP never generates the server-liveness heartbeat TC18 §12.7.9 requires: on Flush_time expiry the RC Server shall emit an AVTPDU from the queue even when that queue is empty, so the RC Client can observe that the server is alive. c-RCP has neither the response queue nor the Flush_time timer to hang this on, and rcp_deadline_monitor_heartbeat() (src/deadline.c, REQ-DL-001) implements only the receiving half — it consumes heartbeats a peer sends. Consequence: an RC Client using a deadline monitor against a c-RCP-based server declares it dead during any idle period longer than the client's deadline, because the server transmits nothing when it has nothing to say.

requirements.title: svr_discovery_timeout register (Table 33, 0x0004, 16 bit, R/W*)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's RC Server functional-configuration model carries no svr_discovery_timeout register (TC18 Table 33, relative address 0x0004, 16 bit, R/W*, microseconds, default 20000 = 20 ms). Consequently the TC18 12.6 rule that an unused discovery stream is dropped after Discovery_TimeOut is not enforced by this library.

requirements.title: RC Server endpoint functional-config block (Table 33) incl. svr_enable always 1 / read-only
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the RC Server endpoint's own functional-configuration block of TC18 Table 33 (svr_ep_len 0x0000 R, svr_ep_enable&clr 0x0002 R/W with svr_enable permanently 1 and read-only, svr_ep_options 0x0003 R/W*, svr_ep_status 0x0004 R/W). The shared rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t prefix models the enable&clr / options octets for ordinary endpoints only, and does not special-case EP0's always-enabled rule.

requirements.title: Register-write outcome: read-only register succeeds silently, write-prohibited register errors
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not distinguish TC18 13.7.1.2's two register-write outcomes at the response level -- a write addressed at a read-only register shall have no effect yet be confirmed with an ordinary (err=0) response, while a write at a write-prohibited register shall produce err=1 with error code UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS. rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() reports writability but no code path maps the two cases onto different response encodings.

requirements.title: Effective register-write payload length = (acf_msg_length - 3) x 4 - pad
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP provides no helper computing the effective number of register-write data bytes as (acf_msg_length - 3) x 4 - pad (TC18 13.7.1.2), the quantity a server needs to know how many octets of an EP0 register write are data rather than address/CRC/padding. rcp_acf_pad_len() computes the pad octet count only.

requirements.title: A sequencer whose state register is manually set to 0 is disabled
requirements.text: A sequencer whose Seq_state register has been manually written to 0 shall be treated as disabled (TC18 §12.7.10 Table 25, relative address 0x0000, 8 bit, R/W): no compound or compound-wait step conditioned on that sequencer shall become executable, and no advance shall move it out of 0 until it is explicitly rewritten to a nonzero state. NOT IMPLEMENTED: rcp_sequencer_set_state() treats 0 as an ordinary state value, so a step whose start_state happens to be 0 fires against a sequencer the client intended to disable, and rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() (REQ-E2E-018) would report a disabled sequencer as "in safe state" if rx_safe_sequencer_state were configured to 0. Distinct from rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() (REQ-SEQ-004), which is the table-wide "zero sequencers implemented" case.

requirements.title: each sequencer is owned by one request stream, and only that stream may access it
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP models no per-sequencer Request_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.10 Table 25, relative address 0x0001, 8 bit, R/W*), the register naming the one RC Client permitted to access that sequencer, and performs no access control on sequencer reads or writes. rcp_sequencer_table_t (include/rcp/request_sequencer.h:85-88) is an unowned array of state bytes and rcp_sequencer_set_state() takes no requester identity. Consequence: any RC Client that can reach the register map can advance or reset any other client's sequencer, including one another client has configured as its rx_safestate_sequencer — a client can therefore forge or clear another client's safe state, defeating the §12.7.7 safety-measure mechanism entirely.

requirements.title: svr_max_sequencers and the sequencer_state table expose sequencer availability and state through the register map
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_general_t.svr_max_sequencers shall equal the count of sequencers the server actually implements (rcp_sequencer_table_t.count), reporting 0 when sequencers are not implemented at all, and the sequencer_state sub-table referenced by rcp_regmap_general_t.sequencer_state shall expose each sequencer's current Seq_state value for reading over EP0 (TC18 §12.7.10). NOT IMPLEMENTED as a wired behavior: both register fields exist (include/rcp/regmap.h:209, 221) but neither is populated from or validated against the live table, and no byte_message_info read path serves the sequencer_state sub-table. Consequence: a client cannot discover how many sequencers a server has, and cannot read a sequencer's state to decide whether a queued conditional step has fired.

requirements.title: evt[2:0] selects which of the six SPI channel configurations a request uses
requirements.text: The SPI endpoint shall carry up to RCP_EP_SPI_MAX_CHANNELS (6) independently pre-configured channel configurations (rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_t::channels), and the configuration a given SPI request executes under shall be selected by that request's evt[2:0] field, per TC18 13.7.3.1/13.7.3.2.

requirements.title: SPI trigger output numbering (Table 38)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 Table 38's SPI trigger output numbering -- signal 0 'SPI execution done', signal 1 reserved, and signals 2..13 pairing each chip select CS0..CS5 with an asserted and a de-asserted event in ascending order. The endpoint models a per-channel trigger selector but derives no trigger signal from CS transitions.

requirements.title: SPI functional-config register block (Table 39) is modeled only in reduced form
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial): c-RCP's rcp_ep_spi_channel_cfg_t does not reproduce TC18 Table 39's per-channel register block. It carries mode/bit_order/cs_polarity/clock_divider/inter_byte_delay_ns/inter_transfer_delay_ns instead of spi_baud_rateN (16 bit, kbit/s), the separate spi_clk_polarityN and spi_clk_phaseN bits, spi_use_csN (common vs per-channel CS), spi_bits_maxN (max consecutive bits without pause), and it expresses lead/trail times in nanoseconds rather than in multiples of spi_clk cycles. spi_ep_len, spi_nr_cs and spi_ep_status are not modeled.

requirements.title: SPI zero-fill when read_size exceeds the payload, full payload on PICO otherwise
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not apply TC18 13.7.3.3's transfer-length rule -- an SPI endpoint shall append zero octets when read_size exceeds the byte_msg_payload length (so the bus clocks read_size octets), and shall still present the whole byte_msg_payload on PICO when read_size is smaller than it. The library's SPI request codec carries payload and read_size as independent fields and derives no transfer length from their relation.

requirements.title: SPI error state resets the EP enable bit; a clamped pin flags every response
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 13.7.3.3's SPI fault latching -- an SPI endpoint that stops execution shall enter an error state recorded in the debug register with its EP_config enable bit reset, requiring the RC Client to clear the error status and re-enable the endpoint before operation continues, and a clamped (stuck-at) IO pin shall raise a flag in the server's diagnostic registers and set the err flag in every subsequent response of that endpoint.

requirements.title: A disabled endpoint still executes configuration requests immediately
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP queues configuration requests submitted to a disabled endpoint (TC18 §12.3.1.3). rcp_server_endpoint_submit() branches only on ep->ep_enable and copies every frame into the pre-load queue when it is false, whereas the specification requires a disabled endpoint to keep executing configuration requests and to queue only operational ones. A client cannot configure an endpoint that is currently disabled -- including writing ep_enable itself.

requirements.title: Queuing a request on a disabled endpoint still emits the requested acknowledge
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not emit an acknowledge when a request is stored for a disabled endpoint (TC18 §12.3.1.3). rcp_server_endpoint_submit() copies the frame into the pre-load queue and returns false with no acknowledge, so a client that asked for an acknowledge receives nothing until the endpoint is enabled and the request eventually executes. The client cannot distinguish a stored request from a dropped one.

requirements.title: Cyclic heartbeat: empty NTSCF-only PDU on an empty response queue
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP models the response-queue periodicity register (rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t::flush_time_us) but does not itself emit the cyclic heartbeat AVTPDU, and in particular never emits the empty PDU -- an NTSCF header carrying no ACF messages at all -- that TC18 13.7.1.1 requires when the flush period elapses with an empty queue. c-RCP is a protocol library, not a scheduler; heartbeat emission is left to the integrator driving rcp_avtp_transport_t.

requirements.title: RC Server trigger signals 0/1: PTP time-sync established and lost (Table 34)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not issue the RC Server trigger signals of TC18 Table 34 -- signal 0 on PTP time-synch established and signal 1 on PTP time-synch lost (signal 2 being t.b.d. in the specification). gPTP lock state is modeled (rcp_timed_admit()'s gptp_locked input) but no trigger source is derived from its transitions, so a triggered request cannot be armed on time-sync events.

requirements.title: A request carried under a TSCF header is postponed until the header's presentation time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not postpone the execution of a request carried under a TSCF header until the header's avtp_timestamp presentation time (TC18 §11.2, §11.2.1). Only the ACF_GBB-embedded presentation_time of §11.2.2.5 is honoured (rcp_timed_due(), rcp_server_endpoint_select_due()); the TSCF header's own avtp_timestamp is used solely as CRC input by rcp_e2e_compute_crc() and never reaches the admission or due-selection path, so standard, conditional and cancel requests arriving under TSCF execute immediately. Consequence: time-scheduled execution via TSCF -- the specification's primary timed-request mechanism -- does not work.

requirements.title: Standard requests, and timed requests under a TSCF header, are sent as ACF_ABB
requirements.text: A standard (best-effort) request shall be encoded as an ACF_ABB message (rcp_acf_encode_abb(), acf_msg_type RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB), and a timed request whose presentation time is carried by an enclosing TSCF header shall likewise be encoded as an ACF_ABB message rather than the ACF_GBB form of TC18 §11.2.2.5, per TC18 §11.2 and §11.2.1. c-RCP currently offers no ACF_ABB timed-request encoder: rcp_timed_encode_request() emits only the ACF_GBB message_timestamp-repurposed variant.

requirements.title: The WakeUp message carries the wake-up source that caused the wake
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's WakeUp message carries no wake-up source (TC18 §12.4.1). rcp_ep_wakeup_encode_wakeup_message() emits a single opcode byte and rcp_ep_wakeup_decode_wakeup_message() returns only the transaction number, whereas the specification requires the repetitive wake response to convey both a WakeUp message and the WakeUp source. The client that requested sleep cannot learn which configured wake source (which sources[] index, wakepin, or network) actually woke the server, which is exactly the diagnostic information the wake-up endpoint exists to provide.

requirements.title: The WakeUp endpoint's functional config carries the WakeUp repetition time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's wake-up endpoint has no configurable WakeUp repetition time (TC18 §12.4.1). rcp_ep_wakeup_functional_cfg_t exposes only the wake-source table, and the handshake in power.c counts attempts without any notion of an interval, so a client cannot configure how often the repetitive wake response is retransmitted. Repetition rate is left entirely to the caller and is neither discoverable nor settable over the protocol.

requirements.title: A refused sleep/standby request is answered with an error response carrying REQUEST_CANCELED
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP answers a refused sleep/standby request with a positive-form SleepCMD response carrying RCP_PWRMODE_ENTRY_REFUSED, not with an error response (TC18 §12.5). The specification requires the rejection to be signalled as an error message with error code REQUEST_CANCELED (RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_CANCELED, include/rcp/errors.h:55). A conformant RC Client watching for an error response never sees the refusal, and a c-RCP client peer is the only thing that can decode the refusal at all.

requirements.title: WakeUp endpoint is fixed to endpoint number 1
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not pin the WakeUp endpoint to endpoint number 1 as TC18 13.7.2.1 requires; rcp_ep_wakeup_* entry points accept any caller-supplied byte_bus_id and the library defines no constant for the fixed WakeUp endpoint index, so the 'only endpoint that stays active in Sleep mode' invariant is the integrator's to uphold.

requirements.title: WakeUp functional-config register block (Table 36) incl. write-1-to-clear wup_status
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP models the WakeUp endpoint's TC18 Table 36 register block only in reduced form -- wup_status is a single boolean latch (rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_t) rather than a 16-bit register whose every bit is one wake-up source and to which writing a 1 clears that bit, and rcp_ep_wakeup_source_cfg_t carries (enabled, active_high) instead of the wup_io_scrN register layout ([10:0] IO pin number, [15:11] IO behavior, pin number 0 terminating the table). wup_ep_len and wup_nr_io_pins_max are not modeled at all.

requirements.title: Wake-up source pin behavior encoding (Table 37)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 Table 37's wake-up source behavior encoding (IO_SRC[15:11]: 0b00000 inactive, 0b00001 rising edge, 0b00010 falling edge, 0b00011 both edges, 0b00100 high level, 0b00101 low level, all other values reserved). rcp_ep_wakeup_source_cfg_t collapses this to (enabled, active_high), which can express the two level modes and 'inactive' but neither edge mode, and rejects no reserved encoding.

requirements.title: The per-stream watchdog is kicked by every request received on that stream
requirements.text: The RC Server's request-reception path shall call rcp_watchdog_keeper_kick() for a request stream's stream_id on every request successfully received on that stream, so that the per-stream watchdog measures the gap between consecutive requests from that RC Client (TC18 §12.7.7, "the watchdog is reset with each request received from this RC Client"). NOT IMPLEMENTED as a wired behavior: rcp_watchdog_keeper_kick() exists and is individually correct (REQ-WDG-003) but has no production call site — only tests call it. Consequence: in an integration built on this library the watchdog overflows on a fixed schedule regardless of client liveness unless the integrator remembers to kick it, which no requirement obliges them to do.

requirements.title: Plain versus safe command mode is selected per endpoint in the generic endpoint config and gates CRC enforcement
requirements.text: Each endpoint shall be addressable in exactly one of two modes selected by a bit in its server-owned generic endpoint configuration: plain command mode, in which requests carry no CRC32 trailer, and safe command mode, in which every request must carry a valid CRC32 trailer and a request without one, or with a mismatching one, shall not be executed (TC18 §13.6). NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's ep_req_crc_enable lives in rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t rather than the generic block, and no code path consults it, so rcp_e2e_unwrap() is only ever invoked by a caller's own choice and a safe endpoint will happily execute an unprotected request.

requirements.title: Safe command mode changes nothing but the appended CRC trailer and the length accounting
requirements.text: A request in safe command mode shall be byte-identical to the same request in plain command mode in its AVTPDU header fields, its ACF message type, its byte_message_info header and its byte_msg_payload, differing only by the appended CRC32 trailer and by the length-accounting adaptation that trailer requires (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_wrap() copies acf_frame verbatim, adapts only acf_msg_length via its private adapt_acf_msg_length(), and appends four octets; rcp_e2e_unwrap() reverses exactly those two steps.

requirements.title: Each ACF message in a multi-ACF AVTPDU carries and is verified against its own CRC32
requirements.text: When an AVTPDU carries more than one ACF message, a separate CRC32 shall be computed, appended to and verified for each E2E-protected ACF message individually, never one CRC across the whole AVTPDU payload (TC18 §13.6). PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_wrap()/rcp_e2e_unwrap() work per ACF message, but no c-RCP code path walks a multi-member frame verifying each member's own trailer — rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() splits members via rcp_sched_split_frame_members() and dispatches them without any CRC check, so a mixed protected/unprotected frame is not handled.

requirements.title: CRC coverage begins with stream_id (8 octets) and avtp_timestamp (4 octets), big-endian
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_compute_crc() shall return the same value as rcp_e2e_crc32() over the concatenation of stream_id as 8 big-endian octets, avtp_timestamp as 4 big-endian octets (IEEE 1722's own field width), and acf_frame[0..acf_frame_len), in that order (TC18 §13.6).

requirements.title: An NTSCF-framed message contributes an all-zero avtp_timestamp to the CRC
requirements.text: When the enclosing AVTPDU carries an NTSCF header (which has no timestamp field of its own), the avtp_timestamp contribution to the CRC32 shall be four all-zero octets (TC18 §13.6). ONLY A CALLER CONVENTION in c-RCP: rcp_e2e_compute_crc()/rcp_e2e_wrap()/rcp_e2e_unwrap() take avtp_timestamp as a plain uint32_t argument with no NTSCF/TSCF discriminator, so nothing prevents a caller from feeding an NTSCF message a non-zero timestamp and producing an interoperability failure that only shows up as a CRC mismatch at the peer.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wrap() adapts acf_msg_length by +1 quadlet before computing the CRC, and rcp_e2e_unwrap() reverses it
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wrap() shall increment the acf_msg_length field of the copy it returns by one quadlet before computing the CRC, so the CRC is computed over the length-adapted frame and a conformant receiver reads a length that already includes the trailer; it shall fail safe (data=NULL, len=0) when the frame is shorter than the two octets holding that field or when the adapted value would exceed the field's 9-bit maximum (0x1FF). rcp_e2e_unwrap() shall decrement it by one quadlet on the copy it returns, so the result is byte-identical to the frame the sender passed to rcp_e2e_wrap().

requirements.title: AVTPDU data length grows by 4 octets for every E2E-protected ACF message it carries
requirements.text: An AVTPDU carrying E2E-protected ACF messages shall have its ntscf_data_length (NTSCF header) or stream_data_length (TSCF header) increased by 4 octets for every ACF message in its payload that is E2E-protected (TC18 §13.6). ONLY IMPLICIT in c-RCP: rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf()/rcp_avtp_encode_tscf() recompute the length field from the payload buffer they are given, so the adjustment is correct only if the caller has already wrapped every protected member; c-RCP provides no function expressing the adjustment and no check that the encoded length matches the number of protected members.

requirements.title: A fragmented message's CRC covers the first fragment's AVTPDU/ACF header plus every segment's payload
requirements.text: For a fragmented request or response the CRC32 shall be computed over the stream_id and avtp_timestamp of the FIRST AVTPDU and the FIRST fragment's ACF header, followed by the concatenated byte_msg_payload of ALL segments in order; the resulting CRC shall be appended only to the last segment's message, and only that last message's acf_msg_length and only that last AVTPDU's data-length field shall be adapted (TC18 §13.6). NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's documented integration wraps only the final fragment's own encoded bytes, so its CRC covers the final fragment's header and payload alone and the earlier segments are entirely unprotected.

requirements.title: The ms bit decides whether a message carries a CRC32 trailer in its last quadlet
requirements.text: A message whose ACF header ms bit is 0 shall carry the CRC32 in its last quadlet, and a message whose ms bit is 1 shall carry no CRC32 at all, the CRC appearing only on the final (ms=0) fragment of a multi-segment message (TC18 §13.6). ONLY A CALLER CONVENTION in c-RCP: rcp_e2e_fragment_carries_crc() takes an abstract is_last_fragment boolean and neither reads the ms bit itself nor is invoked anywhere in src/ — the ms-to-is_last_fragment binding lives only in fragment.h's file header prose.

requirements.title: Requests and responses use one identical CRC scheme
requirements.text: The CRC32 coverage span, parameterization, length adaptation and trailer placement shall be identical for requests and for responses: rcp_e2e_wrap() and rcp_e2e_unwrap() shall take no direction parameter and shall behave identically whichever direction a frame travels in (TC18 §13.6).

requirements.title: A CRC mismatch on a protected stream generates an error response as well as skipping execution
requirements.text: When a request arrives on an E2E-protected stream and its CRC32 does not match, the RC Server shall not execute the request AND shall generate an error response carrying the CRC-mismatch wire error code (RCP_ERROR_POCI_FAILURE, 12 — the code TC18 §12.9.6 Table 27 assigns a CRC mismatch, spelled CRC_ERROR in §13.6's prose) (TC18 §13.6). PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_unwrap() reports RCP_E2E_ERR_CRC_MISMATCH and rcp_e2e_wire_error() maps it, but c-RCP contains no caller of rcp_e2e_unwrap() and no error-response emitter, so the response half never happens.

requirements.title: CRC coverage includes the byte_msg_payload's pad octets and the trailer lands on a quadlet boundary
requirements.text: The CRC32 shall be computed over whole quadlets of the ACF message: the byte_message_info header quadlets and the byte_msg_payload including the 0x00 pad octets acf.h's rcp_acf_pad_len() appends, so that the CRC32 itself occupies the message's final whole quadlet (TC18 §13.6 Figures 19 and 20). NOT ENFORCED: rcp_e2e_wrap() accepts any acf_frame_len of at least 2 octets and appends its 4-octet trailer at that offset, so a caller passing a non-quadlet-aligned (unpadded) frame produces a message whose CRC is misaligned and whose adapted acf_msg_length no longer describes it.

requirements.title: the ADC endpoint's five trigger output signals
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP defines none of the five ADC trigger outputs TC18 §13.7.9.1 Table 50 enumerates. The ADC endpoint shall generate trigger 0 when the averaged output value falls below adc_trigger_min, trigger 1 when it rises above adc_trigger_min, trigger 2 when it falls below adc_trigger_max, trigger 3 when it rises above adc_trigger_max, and trigger 4 when it finishes a measurement interval. ep_adc.h has no trigger enumeration, no threshold registers, and no evaluation function. Consequence: threshold-crossing detection is impossible, and the spec's own documented cyclic-ADC pattern — 'configured to generate responses cyclically ... by using a trigger request which triggers on the ADC EP itself having finished a measurement' (L5033-5034) — cannot be built, because trigger 4 does not exist.

requirements.title: An ADC endpoint serves exactly one channel, is limited to 16-bit resolution, and requires a selected analog input pin
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partially): c-RCP fixes an ADC measurement value at 16 bits (RCP_EP_ADC_VALUE_LEN == 2, ep_adc.h:211) consistent with TC18 §13.7.9.1's 16-bit ceiling, but it does not model the one-channel-per-endpoint rule nor the required selection of an analog input pin for each ADC EP. regmap.h's rcp_regmap_named_signal_t index has no ADC entry, so an ADC endpoint's analog input cannot be bound to a hardware pin through the hw_pin_map table at all. Consequence: an RC Client can configure and read an ADC endpoint that is not wired to any physical input, with no way to discover or set which channel it serves.

requirements.title: ADC inter-sample spacing is one adc_sample_interval, in multiples of adc_base_clk x adc_base_clk_divider
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the ADC sampling cadence TC18 §13.7.9.1 defines. When adc_avg_intervals_per_request x adc_samples_per_avg_interval exceeds 1, successive samples shall be taken one adc_sample_interval apart, where that interval is expressed in multiples of adc_base_clk scaled by adc_base_clk_divider. rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_t carries neither adc_sample_interval nor adc_base_clk nor adc_base_clk_divider, and rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() consumes caller-supplied samples whose spacing this module never constrains. Consequence: the temporal geometry of an ADC response (the entire point of the sample_interval/averaging model) is undefined in this implementation.

requirements.title: ADC sampling occurs only while a request executes, and a compound wait compares the last acquired average without sampling
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 §13.7.9.1's request-gated sampling rule. The ADC endpoint shall sample its input only while a request is being executed, so that no ADC trigger can fire in the absence of a request to sample; and a compound wait request on an ADC endpoint shall not start sampling, comparing instead against the last acquired average value. ep_adc.h provides neither a request-execution state nor any comparison predicate (contrast ep_lin.h's rcp_ep_lin_compare_fires(), REQ-LINEP-002..005). Consequence: continuous monitoring semantics are undefined, and a compound wait targeting an ADC endpoint has no defined match behavior.

requirements.title: adc_ep_len, adc_base_clk, adc_ep_status and adc_base_clk_divider register rows of Table 51
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the ADC functional-configuration block's descriptor, clock and status registers (TC18 §13.7.9.2 Table 51): adc_ep_len (0x0000, 8 bit, R — this description's length in octets), the reserved octet at 0x0001, adc_base_clk (0x0004, 16 bit, R — the ADC system clock), adc_ep_status (0x0006, 16 bit, R/W), and adc_base_clk_divider (0x0008, 8 bit, R/W — generates the ADC_CLK time reference). rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_t is a plain struct holding only the three sampling-pipeline counts. Consequence: a client cannot read the ADC's base clock or status, nor derive ADC_CLK, so no sampling interval can be computed in real time units.

requirements.title: adc_sample_interval, the ADC_CLK cycle count between two samples
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model adc_sample_interval (TC18 §13.7.9.2 Table 51, relative address 0x0009, 8 bit, R/W) — the number of ADC_CLK cycles the endpoint shall wait between two consecutive samples. rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_t carries adc_samples_per_avg_interval, adc_avg_intervals_per_request and adc_combine_avg_values but no interval, and there is no rcp_ep_adc_set_sample_interval() mutator gated by rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable(). Consequence: the sample spacing that §13.7.9.1's worked examples set to 1 us cannot be configured at all.

requirements.title: can_ep_len, can_base_clk and the CAN endpoint's three status registers
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the CAN functional-configuration block's descriptor, clock and status registers (TC18 §13.7.11.2 Table 53): can_ep_len (0x0000, 8 bit, R), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R, reads 0x00), can_base_clk (0x0004, 16 bit, R — the CAN system clock), can_ep_status (0x0006, 16 bit, R/W), the 32-bit CAN EP status at 0x001C (R/W), and the 32-bit FIFO status at 0x0020 (R/W). rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_t holds only bit timings, delay compensation, the execution-delay divider and the XL filter table. Consequence: bus-off, error-passive and FIFO-overflow conditions — the states those status registers exist to report — are unobservable through this endpoint, and the base clock the three bit-timing register sets divide cannot be read.

requirements.title: the CAN endpoint's receive ID filters, which are separate from the CAN XL acceptance filters and valid for all CAN variants
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP conflates two distinct filter tables TC18 §13.7.11.2 keeps separate. Table 53 defines acceptance filters 1..4 (0x0024..0x0030, 32 bit R/W) as 'acceptance filter for CAN XL' AND receive filters 1..4 (0x0030..0x003C, 32 bit R/W) as 'ID filter for frame reception', the latter explicitly 'valid for all CAN variants' per the §13.7.11.2 bullet list. c-RCP implements only one table — rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_t.xl_filters[RCP_EP_CAN_XL_MAX_FILTERS], written by rcp_ep_can_set_xl_filter() (REQ-CANEP-014) — and its own header describes it as the CAN-XL acceptance/ID filter set. Consequence: Classical CAN, CAN FD and CAN FD light traffic cannot be ID-filtered on reception at all through this endpoint; the only filter table available is scoped to CAN XL.

requirements.title: Usage of the new CAN XL physical layer is a functional-configuration setting of the CAN endpoint
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (as configuration): TC18 §13.7.11.2 lists 'usage of new PL (YES|NO) for CAN XL' among the settings the CAN endpoint's functional configuration comprises, i.e. a per-endpoint, runtime-writable choice. c-RCP instead expresses the physical-layer selection per FRAME, as the distinction between RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_CLASSICAL_PL (4) and RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_NEW_PL (5) carried in the ACF evt[2:0] field (ep_can.h:304-311), and rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_t carries no corresponding flag. Consequence: a client cannot read back or constrain which XL physical layer an endpoint is provisioned for, and nothing rejects a frame whose XL variant contradicts the endpoint's actual physical layer.

requirements.title: The FrameFormat selector's numeric code assignment (CBFF 0 through XL new-PL 5, with 6 and 7 reserved)
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_t shall assign exactly the FrameFormat codes TC18 §13.7.11.3 Table 54 fixes: RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_CBFF = 0, RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_CEFF = 1, RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_FBFF = 2, RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_FEFF = 3, RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_CLASSICAL_PL = 4 (XL over the classical physical layer), and RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_NEW_PL = 5 (XL over the new physical layer); codes 6 and 7 are reserved and rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid() shall reject them, causing rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_request()/_decode_frame_response() to return RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_FRAME_FORMAT. The selector shall be carried in the low three bits of the ACF byte_message_info evt field.

requirements.title: Remote frames are not supported, and an 11-bit CAN ID is right-aligned in the CAN ID field
requirements.text: The CAN endpoint shall not support sending remote frames: c-RCP exposes no remote-frame flag, encode function, or decode outcome anywhere in ep_can.h/ep_can.c, so every frame this endpoint encodes or decodes is a data frame. An 11-bit CAN identifier shall be right-aligned within the CAN ID field: rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_request()/_encode_frame_response() write arbitration_id via write_prefix()'s big-endian put_u32() into the fixed 4-octet identifier prefix, leaving the unused high bits zero, and rcp_ep_can_arbitration_id_valid() bounds a base-width identifier at 0x7FF so no bit can escape that alignment.

requirements.title: ISELED read responses are aggregated into one or more ACF messages up to the requested read_size
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 §13.7.12.1's ISELED response-aggregation rule. Responses received from the ISELED network shall be 5/4-bit decoded and aggregated into one or multiple ACF messages, bounded by the read_size the originating read request carried. rcp_ep_iseled_encode_response() (src/ep_iseled.c) encodes exactly the rx_data/rx_len its caller supplies, never reads a read_size, never enforces a ceiling, and has no multi-message emission path. Consequence: nothing prevents an ISELED response from exceeding the octets its request asked for, and the number of ACF messages a read produces is undefined.

requirements.title: iseled_collect_resp, the multi-response-per-ACF collection enable
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model iseled_collect_resp (TC18 §13.7.12.2 Table 55, relative address 0x0007 bit 3, 1 bit, R/W) — the flag that enables collecting multiple ISELED device responses into a single ACF message. rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_t has no such member and there is no rcp_ep_iseled_set_collect_resp() mutator gated by rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_writable(). Consequence: the aggregation behavior §13.7.12.1 describes has no on/off control, so a client cannot choose between one ACF message per device response and one message per chain read.

requirements.title: iseled_nr_leds and iseled_rcv_timeout
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP models neither of the two ISELED chain/reception registers TC18 §13.7.12.2 Table 55 defines. iseled_nr_leds (0x0008, 16 bit, R/W) shall record the number of LED devices in the chain, which bounds the maximum number of responses to expect from a read. iseled_rcv_timeout (0x000A, 16 bit, R/W) shall give a receive timeout in ISELED clock tics after which reception ends and the endpoint returns to IDLE. rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_t declares neither, and no mutator exists for either. Consequence: an ISELED read has no defined completion bound in either the count dimension or the time dimension — the endpoint cannot know when a chain read is finished, nor recover from a non-responding device.

requirements.title: BUG: rcp_ep_iseled_requires_isp_n() has inverted polarity — ISP_N is required exactly when iseled_use_rcv_clk is set
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_requires_isp_n() shall return true if and only if iseled_use_rcv_clk is true. Per TC18 §13.7.12.2, iseled_use_rcv_clk selects using the clock provided by the first ISELED device instead of the FreqSync pattern, and that device-provided clock arrives on the ISP_N pin; the spec states explicitly that it is only when the Freq_Sync pattern is used (iseled_use_rcv_clk false) that ISP_N need not be connected to a physical pin. c-RCP currently returns !use_rcv_clk (src/ep_iseled.c:109-112), which is exactly backwards: it reports ISP_N as required in FreqSync mode (where the spec says it may be left unwired) and as unnecessary in recovered-clock mode (where the clock physically arrives on ISP_N). Consequence: pin-mapping validation built on this predicate will accept an ISELED endpoint in recovered-clock mode with no ISP_N pin bound, leaving the receiver with no clock source.

requirements.title: The LIN transmission-done trigger fires only after the configured trailing time has also expired
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partially): TC18 §13.7.10.1 requires the LIN endpoint's trigger to fire when BOTH conditions hold — the transmission has been finalized AND the configured trailing time has expired. c-RCP's rcp_ep_lin_trigger_fires() (src/ep_lin.c) evaluates only the transmission-finalized half, returning tx_done_event unchanged for RCP_EP_LIN_TRIGGER_TX_DONE, and rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_t declares no trailing-time field for the second half to consult. Consequence: a LIN endpoint configured with a repeated trigger request on its own trigger — the spec's own documented way to send cyclically on the LIN bus — will re-fire before the inter-frame trail time has elapsed, producing back-to-back LIN frames with no gap.

requirements.title: lin_ep_len, lin_base_clk and lin_ep_status register rows of Table 52
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the LIN functional-configuration block's descriptor, clock and status registers (TC18 §13.7.10.2 Table 52): lin_ep_len (0x0000, 8 bit, R — this description's length in octets), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R), lin_base_clk (0x0004, 16 bit, R — the LIN system clock), and lin_ep_status (0x0006, 16 bit, R/W). Only lin_clk_divider (0x0008, 8 bit, R/W) is modelled, as rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_t.lin_clk_divider (REQ-LINEP-011/012). Consequence: a client can write the LIN bit-time divider but cannot read the base clock it divides, so it cannot compute an actual LIN bit time, and cannot read the endpoint's status.

requirements.title: The MDIO EP has no configurable parameters beyond the common block, but still exposes mdio_ep_len and mdio_ep_status
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partially): c-RCP correctly gives the MDIO endpoint no endpoint-specific configurable parameters, matching TC18 §13.7.13.2's 'The MDIO EP does not have any configurable parameters' — rcp_ep_mdio_functional_cfg_t holds only regmap.h's common block. However Table 56 still fixes three register rows c-RCP does not model: mdio_ep_len (0x0000, 8 bit, R — this description's length in octets), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R, reads 0x00), and mdio_ep_status (16 bit, R/W, contents to be defined by the specification). Consequence: the MDIO block is not enumerable at the addresses Table 56 fixes and its status register is unreadable.

requirements.title: the 2-bit mdio_mode selector and the Figure 42 request payload layout
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's MDIO request payload layout does not match TC18 §13.7.13.3. Figure 42 lays the payload out as reserved bits, a 2-bit mdio_mode field, mdio_address, then mdio_payload, where Table 57 gives mdio_mode four meanings — MMD single-word access, MMD multiple-byte access, MMS single-word access (10b) and MMS multiple (double) word access (11b) — and mdio_address follows the IEEE and OA SPI specifications. c-RCP instead uses its own 5-byte prefix of a 1-octet clause selector (RCP_EP_MDIO_CLAUSE_22 / _45), a 1-octet prtad, a 1-octet devad and a big-endian 2-octet regad (ep_mdio.h:137-141), with no mdio_mode field at all and no distinction between single-access and multiple-access modes — its burst behavior is instead carried by a separate 2-octet word_count. Consequence: c-RCP's MDIO requests are not wire-compatible with a conforming peer, and the single-word vs multiple-access selection is inexpressible.

requirements.title: MMS0 and MMS1 carry 32-bit data fields, not 16-bit
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's MDIO data fields are unconditionally 16 bits wide, contrary to TC18 §13.7.13.3 Table 57, which requires 16-bit data fields for MMD accesses and for MMS other than 0 and 1, but 32-bit data fields for MMS0 and MMS1. rcp_ep_mdio_word_encode()/rcp_ep_mdio_word_decode() serialize exactly two octets each, rcp_ep_mdio_pack_len() returns word_count * 2, and rcp_ep_mdio_word_count_of() rejects any odd byte length — none of them consults an access mode. Consequence: MMS0/MMS1 register accesses (the OPEN Alliance SPI/MMS register spaces where 32-bit words are the norm) cannot be encoded or decoded, and a peer's 32-bit MMS payload will be misparsed as two unrelated 16-bit words.

requirements.title: UART RX FIFO overflow is not flagged in a UART EP status register
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the UART endpoint's fifo-rx-buffer nor its uart_ep_status register, and therefore never flags an RX FIFO overflow (TC18 §13.7.8.1). rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_t carries ep_rx_buffer_size (the FIFO's configured length) but no status field, and no c-RCP function sets or reports an overflow condition. Consequence: an RC Client cannot distinguish a short read caused by uart_timeout from one caused by silently discarded, overflowed RX data.

requirements.title: UART read-response completion is triggered by read_size satisfied, uart_timeout expiry, or a full RX FIFO
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement the UART read-request completion rule (TC18 §13.7.8.1) — a read response shall be emitted as soon as (a) the fifo-rx-buffer holds as many octets as the request's read_size, or (b) uart_timeout has expired, or (c) read_size exceeds uart_rx_fifo_size and the FIFO is full, in which case the response shall be fragmented via rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_response_fragmented(). c-RCP supplies the three ingredients (read_size in the ACF header, cfg->uart_timeout_ms, and the fragmenting encoder) but never arbitrates between them; the choice is left entirely to an unspecified caller. Consequence: two conforming c-RCP-based servers can answer identical read requests with materially different response cadence and fragmentation.

requirements.title: UART read_size is narrowed to 8 bits, below the ACF header's 12-bit read_size field
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP narrows the UART read request's read_size to one octet (rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_request()'s uint8_t read_size parameter, ep_uart.h:357), so it cannot express a read_size above 255, whereas the ACF byte_message_info read_size_or_segment_num field is 12 bits wide (0-4095, acf.h:257) and TC18 §13.7.8.1 explicitly contemplates a read_size larger than uart_rx_fifo_size driving a fragmented response. Consequence: c-RCP cannot originate — and rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_request()'s uint8_t *out_read_size cannot faithfully surface — a conforming peer's UART read request in the 256..4095 range.

requirements.title: UART compound wait request comparison against the RX FIFO, bounded by uart_rx_fifo_size
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP provides no UART compound-wait comparison surface (TC18 §13.7.8.1). A compound wait request on a UART endpoint shall respond when the expected data in the request matches the data held in the fifo-rx-buffer, with the compared length bounded above by uart_rx_fifo_size. ep_uart.h has no analogue of ep_lin.h's rcp_ep_lin_compare_fires()/rcp_ep_lin_compare_mode_t, so a compound wait step targeting a UART endpoint has no defined match semantics in this implementation. Consequence: compound requests (TC18 §13.5.1) cannot be evaluated against a UART endpoint.

requirements.title: uart_ep_len, the reserved octet, and uart_ep_status register rows of Table 48
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the UART functional-configuration block's own descriptor and status registers (TC18 §13.7.8.2 Table 48): uart_ep_len (relative address 0x0000, 8 bit, R — the length of this description in octets), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R, reads 0x00), and uart_ep_status (0x0004, 16 bit, R/W). rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_t is a plain C struct with no register-map serialization, so a client walking the EP functional-config table cannot discover this block's length or read its status. Consequence: the UART block is not enumerable or serializable over the wire at the addresses Table 48 fixes.

requirements.title: uart_baud_rate is in kbit/s, uart_stop_bits counts HALF stop bits, and uart_timeout is in bit times measured from the last received stop bit
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (units diverge): c-RCP's UART functional configuration does not use the units TC18 §13.7.8.2 Table 48 fixes. uart_baud_rate shall be a 16-bit R/W field expressed in kbit/s (c-RCP: uint32_t baud_rate with no documented unit); uart_stop_bits shall be an 8-bit R/W count of HALF stop bits, so 1.5 stop bits is the legal value 3 (c-RCP: rcp_ep_uart_stop_bits_t, a two-valued enum ONE=0/TWO=1 that cannot express 1.5); uart_timeout shall be an 8-bit R/W receiver timeout in BIT TIMES measured from the last received stop bit (c-RCP: uint32_t uart_timeout_ms, milliseconds, with no defined measurement origin). Consequence: c-RCP and a conforming peer will disagree numerically on every one of these three registers, and 1.5-stop-bit UART framing is unreachable.

catalogNote: Phase 22 re-certification pass (ROADMAP.md milestone 85, v0.85.0): every requirement below was individually reviewed against the source file its //cfusa:req tag actually appears in (a per-prefix audit, not a blind carry-over) and classified via the "scope" field. scope="tc18" entries (779 of 854) describe the actual implemented TC18 behavior -- register-map access control, lifecycle transitions, E2E CRC32 safe points, per-endpoint-type request/response shapes, discovery, power-mode transitions, and every ADAPT-class satellite -- and are this project's own ISO 26262 ASIL-B safety-case basis going forward. scope="legacy-compat" entries (75 of 854) describe the retired pre-TC18 Zone/Command surface (rcp.h/rcp.c and tests/legacy_mock.* only); they are demoted to level/asil "QM" and their text is prefixed accordingly, but kept -- not deleted or renumbered -- because that legacy surface is out of scope for this milestone to touch (ROADMAP.md's v0.84.0 milestone already confirmed it is the last consumer of those retired types anywhere in src/) and still carries //cfusa:req tags naming these ids; deleting the catalog entries out from under a surviving tag would only trade one inaccuracy (an unqualified legacy requirement) for another (a dangling reference cfusa trace would then report). Only the tc18 subset is this project's claimed certification basis, and it is complete against Phases 13-21 as actually shipped -- not a forward-declared placeholder the way the legacy program's own catalog was at its v0.2.0, since unlike v0.2.0 this catalog was not written before the code it describes. TC18 requirements-corpus completeness pass (v0.105.0): 158 entries were added by a clause-by-clause sweep of TC18 sections 10 through 13.7.13 for normative clauses, tables and figures that no existing entry covered. Every added entry carries a "tc18" field citing the exact section (and the line of the specification text it was read from) and a "status" field: "implemented" (behaviour c-RCP provides, scope "tc18", ASIL-B), or "partial"/"not-implemented" (a normative obligation c-RCP does NOT meet -- scope "tc18-gap", level/asil "QM", text opening with "NOT IMPLEMENTED", and a test that pins the deviation rather than pretending it is absent). A tc18-gap entry is deliberately NOT part of the ASIL-B safety-case basis; it exists so the catalog is an honest map of the specification's normative surface instead of a map of this implementation only.
